question: Eku agba mi, mo ri awon leaf mi ti won n yellow, mo si ri awon small white fly ni abe leaf. Kini mo le se?
answer: Ohun ti o n se apejuwe ni eepi funfun ti gbin (Bemisia tabaci). Eepi funfun n mu 'cassava mosaic virus' wa, ati pe o le fa pipadanu ikore ti o to 70%. Ohun ti o le se: (1) Mu awon ewe ti o ni arun kuro ki o si sun won — ma ko won sinu kompositi. (2) Fun ogba kekere, lo epo neem (5 milimita fun lita omi kan) ti o fi fo labe ewe, ni gbogbo ose meje fun ose meta. (3) Gbin 'sunn hemp' tabi marigold ni eti oko — eepi funfun ko feran awon ohun ogbin wonyi. (4) Ni akoko ti nbo, gbin eya cassava ti o ni idaduro si 'cassava mosaic virus' bii TME 419 tabi TMS 98/0581. Ranti pe oogun ti o lagbara pupo le pa awon kokoro ti o n ran wa lowo, nitori naa ma lo neem tabi ose Dudu nikan. Ti o ba nilo iranlowo siwaju, lo si ile ise agbeko agbegbe re.
source: IITA Cassava Pest Management Guide, 2023; reviewed by Dr. A. Okeowo, agronomist

question: Good evening sir. My tomato leaf get black spot for underside and the fruit dey rot before e ripe. Wetin I fit do?
answer: O dey deal with late blight (Phytophthora infestans). Dis one na serious disease wey fit destroy your whole tomato farm if you no act fast. Wetin to do: (1) Remove every leaf and fruit wey don get black spot — carry them far from the farm and bury them, no put for compost. (2) Spray copper-based fungicide (copper hydroxide or copper oxychloride) at 3 grams per litre of water. Spray both top and bottom of every leaf. Repeat every 7 to 10 days if rain dey fall. Stop spraying 14 days before harvest. (3) Make your farm get good air — if the tomato plants dey too close together, thin them. (4) Next season: plant blight-resistant varieties like 'Tengeru 2010' or 'Mongal F1'. Rotate your farm — no plant tomato or potato for the same place next year. Water the ground, not the leaves, to keep the leaf dry. If you no fit get copper fungicide, ask your agricultural extension agent for help.
source: IITA Tomato Production Guide; reviewed by Dr. B. Adewale, plant pathologist

question: Sannu. Masara ta na da ramuka a cikin ganye, ina kuma ganin tsutsa a jikin ganye na sabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Wannan cuta ce da ake kira fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda), mafi hatsarin kwaro ga masara a Afirka. Kada ka damu da yawa — ana iya shawo kan ta ba tare da magunguna masu tsada ba. Abubuwan da za ka yi: (1) Idan gona karam ce, tara tsutsar da hannu a cikin mazubin masarar ka kuma ka kashe su. (2) A zuba man neem a cikin mazubin (a jiƙa ƙwayayen neem a ruwa dare daya, a tace sannan a fesa). (3) Idan gona babba ce, a yi amfani da maganin halitta kamar Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) — wannan maganin yana kashe tsutsa ne kawai, ba zai cutar da mutum ba. (4) A dasa masara da wuri, kuma a hada shi da wake-wake wanda ke rage yawan kwaro. (5) A guji amfani da magungunan kashe kwaro na roba kawai — juriya ya zama gama gari a Yammacin Afirka. Idan har yanzu kana da matsala, je ofishin noma na karamar hukumar ka.
source: FAO Fall Armyworm Control Guide, 2024; IITA Maize Program

question: Shikamoo. Mahindi yangu hayakua vizuri na majani yana rangi ya zambarau. Nilitumia mbolea ya DAP lakini haikusaidia...
answer: Shikamoo. Rangi ya zambarau kwenye majani ya mahindi inaweza kuwa na sababu nyingi — inaweza kuwa upungufu wa fosforasi, au ugonjwa wa virusi, au hata uharibifu wa mizizi kutoka kwa wadudu wa ardhini. Mimea inayoonyesha dalili za aina moja inaweza kuwa na matatizo tofauti kabisa. Kwa sababu hii, siwezi kukupa utambuzi sahihi kutoka kwa maelezo pekee. Hiki ndicho unachopaswa kufanya: Chukua mimea michache yenye dalili (pamoja na mizizi) na upeleke katika ofisi ya karibu ya kilimo ya kaunti (county extension office) au KALRO. Waambie historia yote — tarehe ya kupanda, mbolea uliyotumia, na mwelekeo wa dalili. Watachunguza na kukupa ushauri sahihi. Usitumie dawa yoyote kabla ya kupata utambuzi sahihi — inaweza kuwa upotevu wa pesa na inaweza kuharibu mazingira.
source: KALRO Maize Diagnostics Protocol; FAO Guide to Nutrient Deficiency Identification

question: Namaste. Dhaan ki pattiyon par bhooray dhabbe hain aur baal aur baal ke dono taraf piliyaan dikh rahi hain. Kya karna chahiye?
answer: Yeh rice blast rog hai (Magnaporthe grisea), jo chawal ki fasal ke liye sabse khatarnak bimariyon mein se ek. Yeh fungus pattiyon, daathon aur danon ko bhi prabhavit kar sakta hai. Iska ilaaj: (1) Prabhavit pattiyon ko turant kaat kar hata dein aur khet se door jala dein. (2) Khet mein paani bhar kar rakhein — fungus pani mein phail nahi sakta. (3) Tricyclazole ya carbendazim-based fungicide ka chidakav karein, 10-14 din ke antraal par, agar bimari zyada faili hai. (4) Agli fasal ke liye: roti pratirodhak kismein lagayein jaise 'Pusa 44' ya 'Swarna', aur beej ko seed treatment avashya karein. (5) Ure ki matra ko sambhal kar rakhein — zyada nitrogen se blast bimari badh jaati hai. Khoon ki kami ho to potash ki matra badha dein. Kshetriya krishi vistar adhikari se sampark karein agar bimari 40% se adhik phasal tak phail gayi hai.
source: ICAR Rice Blast Management Guide, 2024; Punjab Agricultural University

question: Good morning. My cowpea leaves are curling and I see small black insects on the stems and young pods. What can I use that is safe?
answer: The small black insects on stems and pods are cowpea aphids (Aphis craccivora). While they rarely kill the plant by themselves, they transmit mottle virus which can reduce yield by 60%. Here is a safe management plan: (1) For small infestations (less than 20% of plants): spray with neem oil at 5ml per litre of water, or make a soap solution (1 tablespoon of mild liquid soap in 1 litre of water). (2) For larger infestations: apply a botanical insecticide like pyrethrum-based spray. Avoid broad-spectrum synthetic insecticides — they kill the predators that naturally control aphids. (3) Plant a border of sorghum or maize around your cowpea field — this attracts ladybirds and hoverflies that eat aphids. (4) Next season: plant cowpea early (at the start of the rains) to avoid the peak aphid period. Resistant varieties like 'IT90K-277-2' are available from IITA. Do not worry — cowpea aphids are manageable with these methods.
source: CSIR-SARI Cowpea Production Guide, 2023; reviewed by Dr. S. Adjei, entomologist

question: Daalunu. Akwukwo cassava m nwere akara mosaic, osisi anaghị eto nke ọma. Gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: Ọrịa ị na-ahụ bụ Cassava Mosaic Virus (CMD) — ọrịa kachasị njọ nke na-awakpo akpu. Ọ bụ whitefly na-ebute ya. O dighi ogwu ogwu — mgbochi ka mma. Ihe ị ga-eme: (1) Wepu osisi ndị na-arịa ọrịa ma kpochapu ha ozugbo — ejila ha mee kompositi. (2) Tinye osisi ohuru di iche iche na-eguzogide CMD dị ka TME 419 ma ọ bụ TMS 98/0581. (3) Gbaa mbọ hụ na ị na-achịkwa whiteflies — lee usoro whitefly na agri-001. (4) Ejila okpukpu ma ọ bụ mkpu site na osisi ndị na-arịa ọrịa. (5) Gbanwee ala — akụla akpu n'otu ala ahụ ruo oge abụọ. Nye akpu gị nri ọma site na itinye compost ma ọ bụ potaịsh ka osisi wee guzogide ọrịa. Maka enyemaka ọzọ, gakwuru ọrụ ugbo gị.
source: NRCRI Umudike Cassava Disease Guide; IITA Cassava Virology Lab

question: Witamwo. Mango yakwa irutaga nyeki ndune na matunda makamaga na goro. Ndingakora atia?
answer: Nyeki iria uonaga ni nyeje (Bactrocera dorsalis). Itumaga mango ikahiu na goro, na thukuna iria titumaga goro. Ndungata iria: (1) Ona macio mothe marĩ thi. (2) Thondeka mitego iria itagaga nyeki — tunya ndibei (methyl eugenol) na ke ndiria uthua. (3) Ute njege ikahi. (4) Tema na mutu macio marĩ thi, no utikie moto. (5) Wiki irayo, haya moto iria ikaa goro — mathondeko nyeje. (6) Agriria: harambia mitego (pheromone trap) kana matu 10. (7) Kana nyeki nyingĩ, thi na kïrîma na tiri — thi ikuragia nyeje. (8) Kwa mbere ya mwaka mũka: thondeka nyeje itathondeka — tega mango ciamo ciaku thi. (9) Tomia macio maku — nyeje itendaga kũgura mothondekeni. (10) Kana ũkĩona manyeki mongĩ, hoera KALRO kana ministry of agriculture.
source: KALRO Mango Production Guide; ICIPE Fruit Fly Management Brief

question: Sat sri akal. Mere moongphali de pate te gol gol chitthe lag gaye ne. Ki karan hai ate ki ilaaj hai?
answer: Ji, moongphali de patte te gol gol chitthe — iq kaga di bimari hai jo 'early leaf spot' kehlondi hai (Cercospora arachidicola). Eh fungus bimari hai jo pattiyon nu peela kar ke gira dindi hai, jo fasal de jhambe nu ghat dindi hai. Ilaj: (1) Bimari pattiyaan nu tor ke khet toh bahar kadh ke sutt deo (jalao nahi, balke mitti vich dafna deo). (2) Fungicide spray karo — chlorothalonil ya tebuconazole 2-3 gram prati litre paani vich. 10-14 din de antar naal 3 vaar chidakav karo. (3) Vadi bimari ho tan last spray to baad 14 din da wait karke hi vaddi karo. (4) Agle season vich roti de sake ta joth lagao — do saal tak moongphali usi khet vich na lagao. (5) Resistant variety variete lagao jivein 'ICGV 91114' ya 'Punjab 1'. (6) Saaf-suthra beej hi lagao — beej nu thiram fungicide naal treat karke lagao. (7) Phaslan vich haddi da powder paao ta ke potash di kami na hove.
source: Punjab Agricultural University Groundnut Guide; ICRISAT groundnut pathology

question: Oga. My cocoa pod dey turn black, and I fit see white something dey cover am like flour. The pod dey rot inside. Wetin cause am?
answer: Wetin you dey see na black pod disease (Phytophthora megakarya) — na the most serious cocoa disease for West Africa. E fit destroy up to 80% of your harvest if you no act. Wetin to do: (1) Harvest every pod wey don turn black or get white powder — remove them from the tree AND pick them from the ground. Carry them far from the farm and bury them deep (30 cm). (2) Spray copper-based fungicide (copper hydroxide or copper oxychloride at 4g per litre of water). Spray the whole tree, especially the pods. Repeat every 14 days during the rainy season. (3) Prune your cocoa trees — remove lower branches and thin the canopy so sunlight and air fit enter. Wet pods dry faster this way. (4) Maintain shade — too much shade dey keep the pods wet and help the fungus. Remove some shade trees if necessary. (5) Next season: plant tolerant varieties if available from CRIN or your extension agent. Regular harvesting (every 7-10 days during peak season) reduces the number of pods that get infected. No use fungicide wey expire — check the date before you buy.
source: CRIN Cocoa Disease Control Guide; IITA Cocoa Pest Management Brief, 2024

question: Eku oo, mo ri pe awon ewe sorghum mi ti n are showing signs of striga weed. Kini ohun ti mo le se lati gba to?
answer: Eyi je kokoro sorghum shoot fly. Esinsin yi n yin eyin si ori ewe kekere, idin re si n wo inu igi. Imoran: gbin ni kutukutu, tabi lo irugbin ti o lagbara bi SAMSORG 40.
source: NAERLS-Extension, pest/disease advisory for sorghum farmers

answer: விளக்கத்திலிருந்து மட்டும் முழுமையான நோயறிதலை என்னால் சொல்ல முடியாது, ஆனால் கவலைப்படாதீர்கள். பாதிக்கப்பட்ட தாவர மாதிரியை அருகிலுள்ள வேளாண் நிபுணரிடம் எடுத்துச் செல்லுங்கள். அவர்கள் சரியான ஆலோசனை வழங்குவார்கள்.

question: Daalunu. Osisi sorghum m are showing signs of downy mildew. Gini ka m gba mee?

question: Daalunu. Osisi tomato m are showing signs of tomato leaf miner. Gini ka m gba mee?
answer: Nke a nwere ike ịbụ otu n'ime ọrịa ndị na-emetụta tomato. M na-atụ aro ka ị gaa n'ụlọ ọrụ ndụmọdụ ọrụ ugbo dị nso maka nyocha nke ọma. Echela — ọrịa nwere ike ịgbasa ngwa ngwa.
source: NAERLS-Extension, general advisory for tomato farmers

question: Witamwo. tomato yakwa are showing signs of blossom end rot. Ndingakora atia?
answer: Mũtĩ waku ũngĩkorũo na mathĩna ma mĩthemba mĩingĩ. Ũtaara wakwa nĩ ũyũ: oya kĩonereria kĩa mahuti marĩa me na mũingĩ wa magegania, ũkinainie kwa ofici ya ũrimi ĩrĩa ĩrĩ hakuhĩ. Andũ a ũtaũri nĩmakahũria wega. Tiga gũcookerera nĩ ũndũ mũturire ũngĩhota gũkinya mĩtĩ ĩngĩ.
source: ICRISAT dryland crops technical bulletin

question: Nina thina na cassava. Mahuti make are showing signs of root rot. Ndataithie.
answer: Ndagwĩka ũtaũri mwega kuuma macokio macio matiganĩte, no tigwo na njĩra. Oya magegania ma mũtĩ waku ũtware kwa ofici ya ũrimi ĩrĩa ĩrĩ hakuhĩ. Gũtirĩ bata wa gweterera — mathĩna mangĩendana o nginya tũhenio tũngĩ.
source: ICRISAT dryland crops technical bulletin

question: Selam. Ye cocoa behele are showing signs of black pod. Minder adergale?
answer: የሰብልህ ችግር ብዙ መንስኤዎች ሊኖሩት ይችላል። ምክሬ፡ ምልክቱ የታየባቸውን ቅጠሎች ናሙና ወደ አካባቢህ ግብርና ቢሮ ውሰድ። ኤክስቴንሽን ባለሙያ በአካል ካየ በኋላ ትክክለኛ ምርመራ ያደርግልሃል። አትዘገይ — በሽታ በፍጥነት ይዛመታል።

question: Vanakkam. En sorghum are showing signs of downy mildew. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: உங்கள் பயிரின் பிரச்சனைக்கு பல காரணங்கள் இருக்கலாம். என் ஆலோசனை: பாதிக்கப்பட்ட இலைகளின் மாதிரியை அருகிலுள்ள வேளாண் அலுவலகத்திற்கு எடுத்துச் செல்லுங்கள். விரிவாக்க அதிகாரி நேரில் பார்த்து சரியான நோயறிதல் செய்வார். தாமதிக்காதீர்கள் — நோய் விரைவாக பரவும்.

question: Eku oo, mo ri pe awon ewe cassava mi ti n ti n di ofeefee, won si ni awon eebi funfun kekere nisale ewe. Kini ohun ti mo le se lati ko won lo?
answer: This is cassava whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Do NOT spray broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill beneficial insects and make the problem worse. Immediate steps: (1) Remove and burn the worst-affected leaves. (2) Plant sunn hemp or marigold as a border crop — whiteflies avoid them. (3) If more than half the plants are infested, apply neem oil at 5ml per litre of water, spraying ONLY under the leaves, once every 7 days for 3 weeks. (4) Introduce natural predators like ladybird beetles if available in your area.
source: ICRISAT dryland crops technical bulletin

question: Ina fama da matsalar maize ta. Ganyayyakin sun are showing signs of aflatoxin. Taya zan magance wannan?
answer: Mouldy or discoloured grains with a bitter taste are signs of aflatoxin contamination — a toxic fungus (Aspergillus flavus) that can cause liver damage in humans and animals. WARNING: Do NOT eat or sell mouldy grain. It is dangerous. Prevention for this season: (1) Dry harvested grain immediately to below 13% moisture. (2) Sort and remove all discoloured/mouldy grains by hand. (3) Store in clean, dry containers with good air circulation. (4) Use hermetic (sealed) storage bags if available — they cut off oxygen and stop fungal growth. For next season: plant resistant varieties, control insects that damage grain and create entry points for fungus, and harvest early at the right maturity.
source: ICRISAT dryland crops technical bulletin

question: Eku agba mi, cassava mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: This is cassava whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Do NOT spray broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill natural enemies like Encarsia wasps and make outbreaks worse. Instead: (1) Spray insecticidal soap or 0.5% neem oil solution every 7 days for 3 weeks. (2) Remove and burn heavily infested leaves. (3) Plant maize or sorghum as barrier crops between cassava rows to disrupt whitefly movement. (4) Use yellow sticky traps (1 per 10 m²). If infestation persists, apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L as a LAST resort, observing a 14-day pre-harvest interval. Wash hands and produce after application.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, maize mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini mo le se?
answer: Chlorotic streaks following leaf veins indicate Maize Streak Virus transmitted by leafhoppers (Cicadulina spp.). There is no cure. (1) Remove and destroy all affected plants immediately. (2) Plant early at the onset of rains to avoid peak leafhopper populations. (3) Use streak-resistant hybrids: ZM 623, SC 627, or WH 505. (4) Do not plant maize near irrigated vegetable fields, which harbor leafhoppers year-round. (5) Apply carbofuran granules at 1.5 kg a.i./ha to the soil at planting to control early-season vectors. (6) Save seed only from completely disease-free plants.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku agba mi, tomato mi ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Dark spots on leaves with white fungal growth on the underside and rotting fruit indicate late blight (Phytophthora infestans). This disease can destroy a field within DAYS in wet weather. (1) Spray mancozeb (2.5 g/L) OR metalaxyl-M + mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) at 2 g/L, alternating every 7 days. (2) Improve staking and pruning so leaves don't touch soil. (3) NEVER work in the field when leaves are wet. (4) Remove and bury infected plant material away from the field. (5) Plant resistant varieties like Rio Grande or Roma VF. (6) Apply mulch to reduce rain splash. Pre-harvest interval for mancozeb: 5 days.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Mo ni isoro pelu rice mi, awon ewe re ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Grey-whitish lesions on leaves with brown borders indicate rice blast (Magnaporthe grisea). This is the most destructive rice disease worldwide. (1) Avoid excessive nitrogen — limit urea to 60 kg/ha in blast-prone areas and split into 3 doses. (2) Spray tricyclazole at 0.6 g/L or isoprothiolane at 1 ml/L at first sign and repeat after 10-14 days. (3) Maintain 2-3 cm of standing water in the field; intermittent drying stresses plants and increases susceptibility. (4) Plant resistant varieties: NERICA 4, ARICA 3, or IR64. (5) Burn infected straw after harvest — the fungus survives in crop residue.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, cowpea mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini mo le se?
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near cowpea to attract them. (5) If infestation is severe and ants are present (ants farm aphids), apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. Remove ants with a sticky barrier around plant stems first.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, mango mi ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Kini mo le se?
answer: Dark bore holes on fruit and larvae inside the seed indicate mango seed weevil (Sternochetus mangiferae). The adult lays eggs on developing fruit and larvae tunnel into the seed. (1) Collect and destroy ALL fallen fruit and seeds — the weevil completes its lifecycle in the seed. (2) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L when fruit are marble-sized (2-3 cm). Repeat after 21 days. (3) Maintain orchard hygiene: remove and burn fallen leaves and debris. (4) Band tree trunks with sticky bands to trap weevils climbing up. (5) Harvest fruit slightly early (mature green stage) and store away from orchards.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku agba mi, groundnut mi ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Orange-brown powdery pustules on leaves indicate rust (Puccinia spp.). (1) Spray propiconazole at 1 ml/L OR tebuconazole at 0.5 ml/L at first sign. (2) Plant resistant varieties where available. (3) Avoid excessive nitrogen — it promotes lush, susceptible growth. (4) Remove and destroy crop residues after harvest. (5) Practice early planting to avoid peak rust season. (6) Apply balanced NPK (not just urea) to strengthen cell walls.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, yam mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini mo le se?
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit indicate anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). (1) Remove and destroy all infected plant parts — do NOT compost them. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 10-14 days, starting at flowering. (3) Prune to improve air circulation and reduce humidity. (4) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent rain splash. (5) For the next season, use certified disease-free seed and practice 3-year crop rotation with cereals. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, cocoa mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini mo le se?
answer: Holes in pods with frass (insect droppings) indicate pod borer (Maruca vitrata / Helicoverpa armigera). (1) Hand-pick visible caterpillars at dawn. (2) Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) at 2 g/L in the evening — it degrades in sunlight. (3) Apply neem seed kernel extract (50 g/L, soak 12 hrs, strain) weekly. (4) Plant early-maturing varieties to escape peak pest pressure. (5) Install pheromone traps (1 per 0.1 ha) to monitor moth flights. (6) After harvest, deep-plough (20-25 cm) to expose pupae to sunlight and birds. Pre-harvest interval for Bt: 0 days (safe up to harvest day).
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Mo ni isoro pelu plantain mi, awon ewe re ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Stunted growth, yellowing, swollen root galls (knots), and wilting despite moist soil indicate root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.). (1) There is no curative chemical treatment. (2) Incorporate fresh neem leaves or neem cake at 500 kg/ha into the soil 2 weeks before the next planting. (3) Solarize the soil with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks. (4) Plant marigold (Tagetes erecta) as a trap crop — its roots release natural nematicides. (5) Rotate with maize, sorghum, or millet for 2-3 seasons — these are non-hosts. (6) Apply well-composted manure at 5 t/ha; the microbial activity suppresses nematodes.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, sorghum mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini mo le se?
answer: Dead central shoot ('dead heart') in young seedlings indicates shoot fly (Atherigona soccata). (1) Remove and destroy affected seedlings. (2) Apply carbofuran granules at 1 kg a.i./ha in the seed furrow at planting. (3) Sow early at the onset of rains — late-sown crops suffer more damage. (4) Use higher seed rate (12 kg/ha instead of 8) and thin later — this compensates for losses. (5) Apply neem cake at 250 kg/ha at planting. (6) Avoid excessive nitrogen top-dressing during the seedling stage.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, sweet potato mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini mo le se?
answer: Soft, foul-smelling roots indicate root rot caused by soil fungi (Pythium/Phytophthora). (1) Stop watering immediately — wet soil accelerates the rot. (2) Improve drainage by creating raised beds 30 cm high. (3) Remove and destroy all affected plants. (4) Drench the remaining soil with Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg of well-rotted compost. (5) For the next planting season, solarize the soil by covering beds with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks during the hottest months. (6) Rotate sweet potato with maize or sorghum for at least 2 seasons before replanting.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, onion mi ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Kini mo le se?
answer: Soft, rotting bulb base with white fungal growth indicates basal rot (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cepae). (1) Remove and destroy affected plants — do NOT store bulbs from infected rows. (2) Treat seed bulbs with Trichoderma viride (10 g/kg seed) before planting. (3) Avoid injury to bulbs during weeding. (4) Harvest when 50% of tops have fallen and cure bulbs in the sun for 7-10 days. (5) Store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated place. (6) Rotate away from alliums for 4 years.

question: Eku agba mi, millet mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surface with grey-purple fuzz underneath indicate downy mildew (Peronospora spp.). (1) Spray metalaxyl-M + mancozeb at 2 g/L OR phosphorous acid at 3 ml/L every 7-10 days. (2) Improve field drainage and air circulation. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening — water early morning instead. (4) Remove crop debris after harvest. (5) Use disease-free seed for the next planting. (6) For onion, cure bulbs properly (7-10 days in sun) before storage.

question: Eku oo, coffee mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini mo le se?
answer: Holes in stems and 'dead hearts' (withered central shoot) indicate stem borers (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus). (1) Pull out and destroy dead heart plants — larvae inside can spread to healthy plants. (2) Apply crushed neem leaves (1 kg/10 L water, steep 24 hours) into the leaf whorl — repeat weekly. (3) Apply carbofuran 3G granules at 0.75 kg a.i./ha into the whorl at knee-height stage. (4) After harvest, cut stubble to ground level and bury or burn crop residues to kill overwintering larvae. (5) Rotate with legumes (cowpea, groundnut) to break the pest cycle.

question: Mo ni isoro pelu cotton mi, awon ewe re ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Yellowing leaf margins that curl downward ('hopper burn') indicate jassids (Amrasca biguttula). (1) Spray imidacloprid at 0.3 ml/L OR acetamiprid at 0.2 g/L. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L as a repellent. (3) Maintain adequate soil moisture — drought-stressed crops are more attractive to jassids. (4) Use yellow sticky traps (1 per 2 m²). (5) Plant resistant varieties with hairy leaves (hirsutum-type cotton). Pre-harvest interval for imidacloprid: 21 days.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Mo ni isoro pelu tea mi, awon ewe re ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Reddish-brown discolouration of leaves with fine webbing indicates red spider mite (Oligonychus coffeae on tea). (1) Spray propargite at 1 ml/L OR fenazaquin at 1 ml/L ensuring thorough coverage of the underside of leaves. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L every 7 days. (3) Maintain shade — mites thrive in dry, hot, open conditions. (4) Rogue out heavily infested bushes. (5) Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides (especially synthetic pyrethroids) that kill predatory mites. Pre-plucking interval: 7 days.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, cabbage mi ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Kini mo le se?
answer: Seedlings cut at ground level overnight indicate cutworm (Agrotis spp.). (1) Hand-pick cutworms from the soil surface at night using a torch — they hide in the top 2-3 cm of soil during the day and come up to feed at night. (2) Place collars around seedlings: cut the bottom from a plastic cup or use a cardboard tube pushed 2 cm into the soil. (3) Apply neem cake at 50 g per square metre around plants — it deters egg-laying. (4) Sprinkle wood ash in a ring around each plant. (5) Plough the field 2-3 weeks before planting to expose larvae to birds.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Mo ni isoro pelu watermelon mi, awon ewe re ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Soft spots on fruit with small puncture marks and larvae (maggots) inside indicate fruit fly (Bactrocera / Ceratitis spp.). (1) Collect ALL fallen and infested fruit daily — place them in a sealed black plastic bag and leave in the sun for 7 days to kill larvae. (2) Use methyl eugenol pheromone traps (1 trap per 0.1 ha). (3) Apply GF-120 (Spinosad-based fruit fly bait) as spot sprays on a small patch of leaves — do NOT spray the fruit. (4) Bag individual fruits with paper bags when they reach half-size. (5) Plough the soil under the tree canopy to expose pupae. (6) NEVER use unapproved systemic insecticides on fruit crops.

question: Eku oo, cassava mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini mo le se?
answer: This is cassava whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Do NOT spray broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill natural enemies like Encarsia wasps and make outbreaks worse. Instead: (1) Spray insecticidal soap or 0.5% neem oil solution every 7 days for 3 weeks. (2) Remove and burn heavily infested leaves. (3) Plant maize or sorghum as barrier crops between cassava rows to disrupt whitefly movement. (4) Use yellow sticky traps (1 per 10 m²). If infestation persists, apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L as a LAST resort, observing a 14-day pre-harvest interval. Wash hands and produce after application.

question: Mo ni isoro pelu tomato mi, awon ewe re ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Fine webbing and yellow stippling on leaves indicate spider mites (Tetranychus spp.), which thrive in hot, dry conditions. (1) Spray the underside of leaves with a strong jet of water every 3 days to dislodge mites and break webbing. (2) Apply micronized sulfur at 3 g/L or abamectin at 0.5 ml/L. (3) Avoid pyrethroids and broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill predatory mites and trigger mite explosions. (4) Increase humidity around plants by mulching and watering the ground (not leaves) in the morning. (5) For heavy infestation, release Phytoseiulus persimilis predatory mites — 10/m².

question: Eku agba mi, rice mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Bronze-orange discolouration of older leaves ("bronzing") indicates iron toxicity, common in waterlogged, acidic soils. (1) Drain the field for 3-5 days to aerate the soil — this allows iron to precipitate out of the soil solution. (2) Apply lime (2-4 t/ha) to raise soil pH above 5.0. (3) Use NPK 15-15-15 fertiliser rather than single-nutrient fertilisers — potassium helps reduce iron uptake. (4) Plant tolerant varieties: NERICA-L series or TOX 4004. (5) In the next season, avoid continuous flooding of young seedlings; use alternate wetting and drying irrigation.

question: Eku agba mi, groundnut mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Aflatoxin contamination is caused by Aspergillus fungi and is a serious food safety risk — it can cause liver disease. Prevention is everything: (1) Harvest at the right maturity — do NOT delay harvest, especially if rains are expected. (2) Dry produce rapidly and thoroughly to below 13% moisture. Use raised drying racks, not bare ground. (3) Store in hermetic (airtight) bags — PICS bags or metal silos — away from heat and moisture. (4) Sort and discard any grains that are discoloured, shriveled, or moldy BEFORE storage. (5) Apply Aflasafe (biocontrol product available in Nigeria, Kenya) at 10 kg/ha 2-3 weeks before flowering. (6) NEVER feed mouldy grain to livestock.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, yam mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini mo le se?
answer: The yellow-green leaf pattern you describe is Cassava Mosaic Disease caused by geminiviruses transmitted by whiteflies. There is no chemical cure. (1) Uproot and burn ALL affected plants immediately — do NOT use them as planting material. (2) Use certified mosaic-resistant varieties: TME 419, TMS 30572, or IITA-TMS-I011412. (3) Plant stakes at the recommended spacing of 1 m × 1 m. (4) Avoid recycling stakes from infected fields. (5) Intercrop with maize or cowpea to reduce whitefly populations. Contact your nearest IITA or NRCRI extension office for free resistant planting material.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, cocoa mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini mo le se?
answer: Dense clusters of small, distorted shoots ('witches' brooms') indicate Witches' Broom Disease caused by Moniliophthora perniciosa. (1) Prune and burn ALL brooms and infected branches — cut at least 15 cm BELOW the visible broom into healthy wood. (2) Remove diseased pods. (3) Apply copper oxychloride at 3 g/L during flowering to protect new pods. (4) Maintain 40-50% shade — full sun exposure stresses trees and increases susceptibility. (5) Plant resistant cultivars where available (e.g., TSH series). (6) Disinfect pruning tools with 10% bleach solution between trees.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Good evening sir. My plantain get plenty small insect for the leaf. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Holes at the base of the pseudostem and wilting plants indicate banana/plantain weevil borer (Cosmopolites sordidus). (1) Set up pseudostem traps: cut a 30 cm piece of harvested stem, split it lengthwise, and place it cut-side down near the plant. Check and destroy trapped weevils every 2 days. (2) Apply neem cake at 100 g per plant around the base. (3) Remove old, harvested stems at ground level — they are breeding sites. (4) For heavy infestation, drench the soil around the base with chlorpyrifos at 2 ml/L (wear gloves and avoid runoff into water sources). (5) Use clean, weevil-free suckers for the next planting.

question: Hello sir. My onion get plenty small insect for the leaf. I don try some medicine from the market but e no work. Wetin I go do now?
answer: Silvery streaks on leaves and distorted young growth indicate thrips. (1) Spray spinosad at 0.3 ml/L or neem oil at 5 ml/L every 5 days. (2) Use blue sticky traps (thrips are more attracted to blue than yellow), 1 trap per 5 m². (3) Remove weeds from around the field — they serve as alternative hosts. (4) Maintain adequate soil moisture — drought stressed plants are more vulnerable. (5) For heavy infestations, apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L as a soil drench. Pre-harvest interval: spinosad 3 days.

question: Good evening sir. My okra no dey grow well, leaf dey dry. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Yellow vein banding and stunted growth indicate Okra Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus (transmitted by whiteflies). (1) Uproot and burn affected plants immediately. (2) Control whiteflies with neem oil (5 ml/L) + soap every 5 days. (3) Plant resistant varieties: Arka Anamika, Pusa Sawani, or Clemson Spineless. (4) Use yellow sticky traps (1 per 3 m²). (5) Remove weeds from around the field. (6) Delay planting until whitefly populations decline (2 weeks after the onset of heavy rains).
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Good evening sir. My millet get plenty small insect for the leaf. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Discoloured, mouldy grain heads indicate grain mold caused by a complex of fungi (Fusarium, Curvularia, Alternaria). (1) Harvest at the RIGHT maturity — delayed harvest increases mold. Grain should be hard and not produce milky liquid when pressed. (2) Dry grains immediately to 12-13% moisture. Use raised drying racks. (3) Sort and discard all discoloured grains before storage. (4) Store in hermetic (PICS) bags or clean metal containers. (5) For the next season, plant mold-tolerant varieties (e.g., ICSV series for sorghum). (6) NEVER consume or feed visibly mouldy grain — it may contain mycotoxins.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Oga, I get problem for my coffee farm. The plant get plenty small insect for the leaf. Abeg help me out.
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on green berries that turn black and drop indicate Coffee Berry Disease (Colletotrichum kahawae). (1) Spray copper oxychloride at 5 g/L on the developing berries at 4, 8, and 12 weeks after flowering. (2) Prune to maintain an open canopy — this reduces humidity and spore dispersal. (3) Strip and burn all mummified berries remaining on branches after harvest. (4) Apply 2 t/ha of well-rotted compost to improve tree vigour. (5) Plant resistant varieties: Ruiru 11 or Batian (available in Kenya). Pre-harvest interval for copper: 21 days.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Good evening sir. My cotton get plenty small insect for the leaf. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Yellowing leaves that wilt during the day and internal stem browning indicate Fusarium wilt (Fusarium oxysporum). Once a plant shows symptoms, it cannot be saved. (1) Uproot and burn the affected plant with its root ball — do NOT compost. (2) Drench the planting hole with Trichoderma viride (10 g/L) + lime (50 g/hole). (3) Do NOT plant susceptible crops in that spot for 3-4 years — rotate with maize or rice. (4) Solarize the soil during the hottest months. (5) Use resistant varieties (FHIA series for banana). (6) Always use tissue-culture plantlets or certified disease-free suckers for new plantings — the fungus persists in infected planting material.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Hello sir. My tea dey turn yellow with black spots. I don try some medicine from the market but e no work. Wetin I go do now?
answer: Reddish-brown discolouration of leaves with fine webbing indicates red spider mite (Oligonychus coffeae on tea). (1) Spray propargite at 1 ml/L OR fenazaquin at 1 ml/L ensuring thorough coverage of the underside of leaves. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L every 7 days. (3) Maintain shade — mites thrive in dry, hot, open conditions. (4) Rogue out heavily infested bushes. (5) Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides (especially synthetic pyrethroids) that kill predatory mites. Pre-plucking interval: 7 days.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Oga, I get problem for my oil palm farm. The plant get plenty small insect for the leaf. Abeg help me out.
answer: Oga, I no fit give exact diagnosis from only description — plenty crop problem fit look the same. But no worry! Carry sample go your nearest extension office make dem check am well. Quick action dey important!

question: Oga, I get problem for my amaranth farm. The plant dey turn yellow with black spots. Abeg help me out.
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near amaranth to attract them. (5) If infestation is severe and ants are present (ants farm aphids), apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. Remove ants with a sticky barrier around plant stems first.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Good evening sir. My cabbage dey turn yellow with black spots. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near cabbage to attract them. question: Hello sir. My watermelon dey turn yellow with black spots. I don try some medicine from the market but e no work. Wetin I go do now?
answer: White powdery coating on leaves indicates powdery mildew (Erysiphales). It reduces photosynthesis and weakens plants. (1) Spray sulfur-based fungicide (micronized sulfur at 3 g/L) or potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) every 7 days. (2) Improve air circulation by wider spacing and removing excess foliage. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation — water at the base of plants. (4) Spray a solution of 1 part milk to 9 parts water — milk proteins have antifungal properties effective against powdery mildew. Apply weekly. (5) Remove and burn heavily infected leaves. Pre-harvest interval for sulfur: 1 day.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Good evening sir. My cashew get plenty small insect for the leaf. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Holes in nuts and larvae feeding inside indicate cashew weevil. (1) Collect and destroy all fallen nuts and those remaining on the tree — they harbour larvae. (2) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L when nuts are in the early development stage. (3) Maintain ground hygiene: remove leaf litter and debris under trees. (4) Band tree trunks with sticky barriers. (5) Deep-plough under tree canopies after harvest to expose pupating weevils. Pre-harvest interval: 14 days.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Good evening sir. My cassava get plenty small insect for the leaf. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Brown leaf spots on cassava are caused by Cercospora fungi. (1) Remove severely infected lower leaves and burn them. (2) Spray mancozeb (2 g/L of water) or copper oxychloride (3 g/L) every 10-14 days during wet weather. (3) Improve air circulation by widening plant spacing to 1 m × 1 m. (4) Apply mulch to prevent rain splash that spreads spores. (5) For the next crop, choose a well-drained field and apply 2 t/ha of well-rotted compost to strengthen plant resistance. Fungicide pre-harvest interval: minimum 21 days.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Oga, I get problem for my maize farm. The plant get plenty small insect for the leaf. Abeg help me out.
answer: Aflatoxin contamination is caused by Aspergillus fungi and is a serious food safety risk — it can cause liver disease. Prevention is everything: (1) Harvest at the right maturity — do NOT delay harvest, especially if rains are expected. (2) Dry produce rapidly and thoroughly to below 13% moisture. Use raised drying racks, not bare ground. (3) Store in hermetic (airtight) bags — PICS bags or metal silos — away from heat and moisture. (4) Sort and discard any grains that are discoloured, shriveled, or moldy BEFORE storage. (5) Apply Aflasafe (biocontrol product available in Nigeria, Kenya) at 10 kg/ha 2-3 weeks before flowering. (6) NEVER feed mouldy grain to livestock.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Hello sir. My tomato get plenty small insect for the leaf. I don try some medicine from the market but e no work. Wetin I go do now?
answer: Fine webbing and yellow stippling on leaves indicate spider mites (Tetranychus spp.), which thrive in hot, dry conditions. (1) Spray the underside of leaves with a strong jet of water every 3 days to dislodge mites and break webbing. (2) Apply micronized sulfur at 3 g/L or abamectin at 0.5 ml/L. (3) Avoid pyrethroids and broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill predatory mites and trigger mite explosions. (4) Increase humidity around plants by mulching and watering the ground (not leaves) in the morning. (5) For heavy infestation, release Phytoseiulus persimilis predatory mites — 10/m².
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Hello sir. My rice no dey grow well, leaf dey dry. I don try some medicine from the market but e no work. Wetin I go do now?
answer: Holes in stems and 'dead hearts' (withered central shoot) indicate stem borers (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus). (1) Pull out and destroy dead heart plants — larvae inside can spread to healthy plants. (2) Apply crushed neem leaves (1 kg/10 L water, steep 24 hours) into the leaf whorl — repeat weekly. (3) Apply carbofuran 3G granules at 0.75 kg a.i./ha into the whorl at knee-height stage. (4) After harvest, cut stubble to ground level and bury or burn crop residues to kill overwintering larvae. (5) Rotate with legumes (cowpea, groundnut) to break the pest cycle.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Good evening sir. My mango dey turn yellow with black spots. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Soft spots on fruit with small puncture marks and larvae (maggots) inside indicate fruit fly (Bactrocera / Ceratitis spp.). (1) Collect ALL fallen and infested fruit daily — place them in a sealed black plastic bag and leave in the sun for 7 days to kill larvae. (2) Use methyl eugenol pheromone traps (1 trap per 0.1 ha). (3) Apply GF-120 (Spinosad-based fruit fly bait) as spot sprays on a small patch of leaves — do NOT spray the fruit. (4) Bag individual fruits with paper bags when they reach half-size. (5) Plough the soil under the tree canopy to expose pupae. (6) NEVER use unapproved systemic insecticides on fruit crops.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Hello sir. My groundnut dey turn yellow with black spots. I don try some medicine from the market but e no work. Wetin I go do now?
answer: Soft, foul-smelling roots indicate root rot caused by soil fungi (Pythium/Phytophthora). (1) Stop watering immediately — wet soil accelerates the rot. (2) Improve drainage by creating raised beds 30 cm high. (3) Remove and destroy all affected plants. (4) Drench the remaining soil with Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg of well-rotted compost. (5) For the next planting season, solarize the soil by covering beds with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks during the hottest months. (6) Rotate groundnut with maize or sorghum for at least 2 seasons before replanting.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Good evening sir. My yam get plenty small insect for the leaf. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Stunted growth, yellowing, swollen root galls (knots), and wilting despite moist soil indicate root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.). (1) There is no curative chemical treatment. (2) Incorporate fresh neem leaves or neem cake at 500 kg/ha into the soil 2 weeks before the next planting. (3) Solarize the soil with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks. (4) Plant marigold (Tagetes erecta) as a trap crop — its roots release natural nematicides. (5) Rotate with maize, sorghum, or millet for 2-3 seasons — these are non-hosts. (6) Apply well-composted manure at 5 t/ha; the microbial activity suppresses nematodes.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Hello sir. My cocoa get plenty small insect for the leaf. I don try some medicine from the market but e no work. Wetin I go do now?
answer: Black, rotting pods covered with whitish fungal growth indicate black pod disease (Phytophthora megakarya / P. palmivora) — the most damaging disease of cocoa. (1) Remove ALL infected pods immediately — they produce spores that spread to healthy pods. Bury them 30 cm deep away from the farm. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L OR metalaxyl + copper at 2 g/L on ALL pods every 3 weeks during the rainy season. (3) Prune shade trees — too much shade (over 50%) creates high humidity that favours the disease. (4) Harvest pods as soon as they show yellow colour — do NOT let them over-ripen on the tree. Pre-harvest interval for copper: 14 days.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Good evening sir. My plantain dey turn yellow with black spots. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Holes at the base of the pseudostem and wilting plants indicate banana/plantain weevil borer (Cosmopolites sordidus). (1) Set up pseudostem traps: cut a 30 cm piece of harvested stem, split it lengthwise, and place it cut-side down near the plant. Check and destroy trapped weevils every 2 days. (2) Apply neem cake at 100 g per plant around the base. (3) Remove old, harvested stems at ground level — they are breeding sites. (4) For heavy infestation, drench the soil around the base with chlorpyrifos at 2 ml/L (wear gloves and avoid runoff into water sources). (5) Use clean, weevil-free suckers for the next planting.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Good evening sir. My onion no dey grow well, leaf dey dry. Wetin I fit do?
answer: Soft, rotting bulb base with white fungal growth indicates basal rot (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cepae). (1) Remove and destroy affected plants — do NOT store bulbs from infected rows. (2) Treat seed bulbs with Trichoderma viride (10 g/kg seed) before planting. (3) Avoid injury to bulbs during weeding. (4) Harvest when 50% of tops have fallen and cure bulbs in the sun for 7-10 days. (5) Store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated place. (6) Rotate away from alliums for 4 years.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Oga, I get problem for my pepper farm. The plant get plenty small insect for the leaf. Abeg help me out.
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit indicate anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). (1) Remove and destroy all infected plant parts — do NOT compost them. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 10-14 days, starting at flowering. (3) Prune to improve air circulation and reduce humidity. (4) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent rain splash. (5) For the next season, use certified disease-free seed and practice 3-year crop rotation with cereals. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Oga, I get problem for my okra farm. The plant no dey grow well, leaf dey dry. Abeg help me out.
answer: Holes in developing pods with black frass indicate fruit borer (Earias spp. / Helicoverpa armigera). (1) Hand-pick caterpillars at dawn. (2) Spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) at 2 g/L in the evening every 7 days. (3) Apply neem seed kernel extract (50 g/L). (4) Install pheromone traps at 5 traps/ha. (5) Plant trap crop: maize rows around okra to attract borers away. (6) Remove crop residues after harvest and deep-plough.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Hello sir. My millet get plenty small insect for the leaf. I don try some medicine from the market but e no work. Wetin I go do now?
answer: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surface with grey-purple fuzz underneath indicate downy mildew (Peronospora spp.). (1) Spray metalaxyl-M + mancozeb at 2 g/L OR phosphorous acid at 3 ml/L every 7-10 days. (2) Improve field drainage and air circulation. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening — water early morning instead. (4) Remove crop debris after harvest. (5) Use disease-free seed for the next planting. (6) For onion, cure bulbs properly (7-10 days in sun) before storage.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. cotton na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Angular, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown indicate bacterial blight (Xanthomonas spp.). (1) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L + streptomycin at 0.3 g/L at first sign. (2) Avoid working in the field when plants are wet — bacteria spread through water. (3) Use only acid-delinted, certified seed. (4) Rotate with maize or sorghum for 2-3 years. (5) Remove and burn all crop residues after harvest. (6) Avoid excessive nitrogen which promotes lush, susceptible growth.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina fama da matsalar tea ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Translucent blisters on young leaves that turn brown and break indicate Blister Blight (Exobasidium vexans). (1) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L OR hexaconazole at 1 ml/L every 7-10 days during monsoon. (2) Maintain adequate shade (50-60%) — direct sunlight makes blister blight worse. (3) Pluck and destroy all affected leaves. (4) Apply balanced NPK (YTD or similar tea mixture) at recommended rates to maintain bush health. (5) Prune to maintain plucking table height — do NOT allow bushes to become too tall and dense. Pre-plucking interval: copper 7 days.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina fama da matsalar oil palm ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Yellowing patterns on oil palm indicate nutrient deficiency. (1) For nitrogen deficiency (uniform yellowing of older leaves): apply urea at 1-2 kg per tree per year, split into 2 applications. (2) For potassium deficiency (orange spotting on older leaves): apply muriate of potash at 2-3 kg per tree per year. (3) For magnesium deficiency (yellowing between veins of older leaves): apply kieserite at 0.5-1 kg per tree. (4) Apply empty fruit bunch (EFB) mulch at 60 t/ha around palms — it slowly releases nutrients. (5) Conduct a leaf analysis (take leaf #17 from 20 palms) to confirm which nutrients are deficient before large-scale fertiliser application.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina fama da matsalar amaranth ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Brown spots on amaranth leaves indicate leaf spot disease (Cercospora / Alternaria spp.). (1) Remove and destroy affected leaves. (2) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR copper oxychloride at 3 g/L every 10-14 days. (3) Improve air circulation through wider spacing. (4) Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet. (5) Apply well-rotted compost at 2 t/ha to boost plant immunity. (6) Rotate with non-host crops for 2 seasons.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. cabbage na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Small holes in leaves and green caterpillars that wriggle violently when disturbed indicate diamondback moth (Plutella xylostella). (1) Spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki) at 2 g/L every 7 days — it targets caterpillars only. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (3) Use pheromone traps to monitor moth populations. (4) Rotate insecticide groups — diamondback moth rapidly develops resistance. Alternate Bt with spinosad at 0.3 ml/L. (5) Remove and destroy crop residues after harvest. (6) Plant trap crop: Indian mustard attracts moths away from cabbage.

question: Ina fama da matsalar cashew ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Brown, necrotic spots on leaves and dieback of young shoots indicate Tea Mosquito Bug (Helopeltis spp.). (1) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L OR quinalphos at 2 ml/L, targeting the new flush. (2) Maintain adequate shade (50-60%) — open areas suffer more damage. (3) Remove alternative host plants (especially guava, cashew) near the tea field. (4) Prune affected shoots and burn them. (5) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L as a repellent. Pre-harvest interval (plucking): lambda-cyhalothrin 7 days.

question: Sannu. cassava na ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Me zan yi?
answer: The yellow-green leaf pattern you describe is Cassava Mosaic Disease caused by geminiviruses transmitted by whiteflies. There is no chemical cure. (1) Uproot and burn ALL affected plants immediately — do NOT use them as planting material. (2) Use certified mosaic-resistant varieties: TME 419, TMS 30572, or IITA-TMS-I011412. (3) Plant stakes at the recommended spacing of 1 m × 1 m. (4) Avoid recycling stakes from infected fields. (5) Intercrop with maize or cowpea to reduce whitefly populations. Contact your nearest IITA or NRCRI extension office for free resistant planting material.

question: Ina fama da matsalar maize ta. Ganyayyakin sun ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Yellowing of lower leaves (starting at the tip and moving inward in a V shape on maize) indicates nitrogen deficiency. (1) Apply urea (46-0-0) at the rate of 50 kg/ha — split into two doses: half at 3 weeks after planting, half at 6 weeks. Place fertiliser in a band 5 cm from the plant and 3 cm deep — do NOT leave it on the soil surface. (2) Alternatively, apply well-composted poultry manure at 5 t/ha. (3) Intercrop with cowpea or groundnut — they fix atmospheric nitrogen into the soil for your maize. (4) Do NOT apply urea when the soil is dry; wait until after rainfall or irrigate lightly.

question: Sannu. rice na ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Me zan yi?
answer: Oval brown spots on leaves indicate brown spot (Cochliobolus miyabeanus), often associated with nutrient deficiency, especially silicon. (1) Apply potassium silicate at 2 ml/L foliar spray — this strengthens leaf cell walls. (2) Apply balanced NPK (15-15-15) at 200 kg/ha if the crop appears yellowish overall. (3) Spray propiconazole at 1 ml/L if spots cover >10% of leaf area. (4) Avoid water stress — maintain 2-5 cm standing water. (5) For the next season, incorporate rice husks into the soil to increase silicon availability.

question: Sannu. groundnut na suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Me zan yi?
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near groundnut to attract them. (5) If infestation is severe and ants are present (ants farm aphids), apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. Remove ants with a sticky barrier around plant stems first.

question: Sannu. yam na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit indicate anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). (1) Remove and destroy all infected plant parts — do NOT compost them. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 10-14 days, starting at flowering. (3) Prune to improve air circulation and reduce humidity. (4) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent rain splash. (5) For the next season, use certified disease-free seed and practice 3-year crop rotation with cereals. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.

question: Sannu. cocoa na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Holes in pods with frass (insect droppings) indicate pod borer (Maruca vitrata / Helicoverpa armigera). (1) Hand-pick visible caterpillars at dawn. (2) Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) at 2 g/L in the evening — it degrades in sunlight. (3) Apply neem seed kernel extract (50 g/L, soak 12 hrs, strain) weekly. (4) Plant early-maturing varieties to escape peak pest pressure. (5) Install pheromone traps (1 per 0.1 ha) to monitor moth flights. (6) After harvest, deep-plough (20-25 cm) to expose pupae to sunlight and birds. Pre-harvest interval for Bt: 0 days (safe up to harvest day).
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. plantain na suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Me zan yi?
answer: Dark brown streaks that enlarge to black spots on leaves indicate Black Sigatoka (Mycosphaerella fijiensis). This disease can reduce yield by 50%+. ALTERNATE fungicides to prevent resistance. (3) Improve drainage — standing water increases spore production. question: Sannu. sorghum na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surface with grey-purple fuzz underneath indicate downy mildew (Peronospora spp.). (1) Spray metalaxyl-M + mancozeb at 2 g/L OR phosphorous acid at 3 ml/L every 7-10 days. (2) Improve field drainage and air circulation. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening — water early morning instead. (4) Remove crop debris after harvest. (5) Use disease-free seed for the next planting. (6) For onion, cure bulbs properly (7-10 days in sun) before storage.

question: Ina fama da matsalar banana ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Upright, crowded leaves with a 'bunchy' appearance and dark green streaking on petioles indicate Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV) transmitted by the banana aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa). There is NO cure. (1) Uproot and destroy the entire plant including the corm — bury or burn it. (2) Control the aphid vector by spraying imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L on all surrounding plants. (3) Never use suckers from an affected field for new plantings. (4) Use tissue-culture plantlets — they are guaranteed virus-free. (5) Contact your agricultural extension office to report BBTV — it is a notifiable disease in most countries. (6) Quarantine any new planting material for 4 weeks.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina fama da matsalar sweet potato ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Distorted, mottled leaves and stunted growth on sweet potato indicate a viral infection, often transmitted by aphids or whiteflies. (1) Remove and destroy affected plants — viruses cannot be cured. (2) Control the insect vectors with neem oil (5 ml/L) or imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. (3) Use only certified virus-free planting material (vine cuttings or slips). (4) Remove weeds (especially morning glory and other Ipomoea species) that harbour the virus. (5) Plant a barrier crop (maize or sorghum) to disrupt insect movement into the field. (6) Wash hands and tools before handling healthy plants.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. onion na ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Me zan yi?
answer: Purple-brown oval lesions on leaves and flower stalks indicate purple blotch (Alternaria porri). (1) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR iprodione at 1.5 g/L every 10 days. (2) Avoid excessive nitrogen — apply NPK 10-10-20 rather than high-nitrogen fertilisers. (3) Ensure good field drainage. (4) Rotate with non-allium crops for 3 years. (5) Harvest bulbs only when necks are fully dry; cure properly before storage. Pre-harvest interval: mancozeb 7 days.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. okra na ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Me zan yi?
answer: White powdery coating on leaves indicates powdery mildew (Erysiphales). It reduces photosynthesis and weakens plants. (1) Spray sulfur-based fungicide (micronized sulfur at 3 g/L) or potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) every 7 days. (2) Improve air circulation by wider spacing and removing excess foliage. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation — water at the base of plants. (4) Spray a solution of 1 part milk to 9 parts water — milk proteins have antifungal properties effective against powdery mildew. Apply weekly. (5) Remove and burn heavily infected leaves. Pre-harvest interval for sulfur: 1 day.

question: Ina fama da matsalar millet ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Orange-brown powdery pustules on leaves indicate rust (Puccinia spp.). (1) Spray propiconazole at 1 ml/L OR tebuconazole at 0.5 ml/L at first sign. (2) Plant resistant varieties where available. (3) Avoid excessive nitrogen — it promotes lush, susceptible growth. (4) Remove and destroy crop residues after harvest. (5) Practice early planting to avoid peak rust season. (6) Apply balanced NPK (not just urea) to strengthen cell walls.

question: Sannu. coffee na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Holes in stems and 'dead hearts' (withered central shoot) indicate stem borers (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus). (1) Pull out and destroy dead heart plants — larvae inside can spread to healthy plants. (2) Apply crushed neem leaves (1 kg/10 L water, steep 24 hours) into the leaf whorl — repeat weekly. (3) Apply carbofuran 3G granules at 0.75 kg a.i./ha into the whorl at knee-height stage. (4) After harvest, cut stubble to ground level and bury or burn crop residues to kill overwintering larvae. (5) Rotate with legumes (cowpea, groundnut) to break the pest cycle.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina fama da matsalar cotton ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Angular, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown indicate bacterial blight (Xanthomonas spp.). (1) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L + streptomycin at 0.3 g/L at first sign. (2) Avoid working in the field when plants are wet — bacteria spread through water. (3) Use only acid-delinted, certified seed. (4) Rotate with maize or sorghum for 2-3 years. (5) Remove and burn all crop residues after harvest. (6) Avoid excessive nitrogen which promotes lush, susceptible growth.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. tea na suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Me zan yi?
answer: Reddish-brown discolouration of leaves with fine webbing indicates red spider mite (Oligonychus coffeae on tea). (1) Spray propargite at 1 ml/L OR fenazaquin at 1 ml/L ensuring thorough coverage of the underside of leaves. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L every 7 days. (3) Maintain shade — mites thrive in dry, hot, open conditions. (4) Rogue out heavily infested bushes. (5) Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides (especially synthetic pyrethroids) that kill predatory mites. Pre-plucking interval: 7 days.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. oil palm na ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Me zan yi?
answer: Brown spots on oil palm leaves indicate leaf spot disease (Cercospora / Alternaria spp.). (1) Remove and destroy affected leaves. (2) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR copper oxychloride at 3 g/L every 10-14 days. (3) Improve air circulation through wider spacing. (4) Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet. (5) Apply well-rotted compost at 2 t/ha to boost plant immunity. (6) Rotate with non-host crops for 2 seasons.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina fama da matsalar cabbage ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Seedlings cut at ground level overnight indicate cutworm (Agrotis spp.). (1) Hand-pick cutworms from the soil surface at night using a torch — they hide in the top 2-3 cm of soil during the day and come up to feed at night. (2) Place collars around seedlings: cut the bottom from a plastic cup or use a cardboard tube pushed 2 cm into the soil. (3) Apply neem cake at 50 g per square metre around plants — it deters egg-laying. (4) Sprinkle wood ash in a ring around each plant. (5) Plough the field 2-3 weeks before planting to expose larvae to birds.

question: Ina fama da matsalar cassava ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: This is cassava whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Do NOT spray broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill natural enemies like Encarsia wasps and make outbreaks worse. Instead: (1) Spray insecticidal soap or 0.5% neem oil solution every 7 days for 3 weeks. (2) Remove and burn heavily infested leaves. (3) Plant maize or sorghum as barrier crops between cassava rows to disrupt whitefly movement. (4) Use yellow sticky traps (1 per 10 m²). If infestation persists, apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L as a LAST resort, observing a 14-day pre-harvest interval. Wash hands and produce after application.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina fama da matsalar maize ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: The small holes and shredded young leaves indicate fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda). Act immediately — one larva can destroy 3 whorls. (1) Hand-pick and crush egg masses (fuzzy white patches) and visible larvae, especially at dawn or dusk. (2) Apply a 5% neem seed extract (50 g ground neem seed per litre of water, soak 12 hrs, strain) into the whorl of each plant — the larvae ingest it and stop feeding within hours. (3) In maize, add dry sand or ash (1 pinch per whorl) — it desiccates the larvae. (4) As a last resort, apply emamectin benzoate at 0.4 ml/L or spinosad at 0.3 ml/L. (5) Push-pull: plant Desmodium between rows to repel moths and Napier grass around fields to trap them. Pre-harvest interval for spinosad: 3 days.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Habari. Nina shida na tomato. Majani yana yana wadudu wadogo kwenye majani. Nisaidie tafadhali.
answer: Winding tunnels (mines) inside leaves indicate leaf miner (Tuta absoluta / Liriomyza spp.). (1) Remove and destroy mined leaves immediately — each leaf may contain 3-5 larvae. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L with a few drops of liquid soap as a sticker, every 5-7 days. (3) Use pheromone traps (Delta traps with Tuta lure) at 20 traps/ha. (4) Apply spinosad at 0.3 ml/L if infestation exceeds 5% of leaves. (5) Remove all crop debris after harvest and solarize the soil. (6) For greenhouse crops, use insect-proof (50-mesh) netting.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Shikamoo. rice zangu yanageuka manjano na madoa meusi. Nifanye nini?
answer: Bronze-orange discolouration of older leaves ("bronzing") indicates iron toxicity, common in waterlogged, acidic soils. (1) Drain the field for 3-5 days to aerate the soil — this allows iron to precipitate out of the soil solution. (2) Apply lime (2-4 t/ha) to raise soil pH above 5.0. (3) Use NPK 15-15-15 fertiliser rather than single-nutrient fertilisers — potassium helps reduce iron uptake. (4) Plant tolerant varieties: NERICA-L series or TOX 4004. (5) In the next season, avoid continuous flooding of young seedlings; use alternate wetting and drying irrigation.

question: Shikamoo. groundnut zangu yana wadudu wadogo kwenye majani. Nifanye nini?
answer: Soft, foul-smelling roots indicate root rot caused by soil fungi (Pythium/Phytophthora). (1) Stop watering immediately — wet soil accelerates the rot. (2) Improve drainage by creating raised beds 30 cm high. (3) Remove and destroy all affected plants. (4) Drench the remaining soil with Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg of well-rotted compost. (5) For the next planting season, solarize the soil by covering beds with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks during the hottest months. (6) Rotate groundnut with maize or sorghum for at least 2 seasons before replanting.

question: Habari. Nina shida na yam. Majani yana yana wadudu wadogo kwenye majani. Nisaidie tafadhali.
answer: Holes in leaves and tubers indicate yam beetle (Heteroligus spp.). (1) Hand-pick beetles at night when they are active and visible with a torch. (2) Apply carbofuran granules at 1.0 kg a.i./ha to the soil around the mounds at planting. (3) Delay planting until after the first heavy rains when beetle populations naturally decline. (4) Hill up (re-mound) yam mounds to expose beetles and their eggs. (5) Plant resistant varieties: Dioscorea rotundata cultivars show better tolerance. (6) After harvest, deep-plough to expose overwintering beetles to predators.

question: Shikamoo. cocoa zangu yanageuka manjano na madoa meusi. Nifanye nini?
answer: Sunken, black lesions on young shoots and pods indicate mirids/capsids (Sahlbergella singularis). (1) Spray imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L OR bifenthrin at 1 ml/L, targeting the canopy thoroughly. (2) Remove and burn heavily damaged shoots and pods. (3) Maintain adequate canopy shade — mirids prefer open, exposed canopies. (4) Avoid excessive pruning that exposes the tree interior. (5) Monitor weekly with a beating tray or by tapping branches over a white cloth to count insects. Treat when you find >4 mirids per 10 taps.

question: Habari. Nina shida na coffee. Majani yana yana wadudu wadogo kwenye majani. Nisaidie tafadhali.
answer: White, cottony masses on stems, leaves, and fruit indicate mealybugs. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml/L) + neem oil (5 ml/L) every 5 days. (2) Remove heavily infested branches and burn them. (3) Control ants — they protect mealybugs from natural enemies. Apply a sticky band around the trunk. (4) Release Cryptolaemus montrouzieri (mealybug destroyer) ladybirds at 10-20 per tree. (5) Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill natural enemies. (6) For severe infestation, apply imidacloprid as a soil drench (NOT a foliar spray).

question: Shikamoo. cotton zangu hayakui vizuri, majani yanakauka. Nifanye nini?
answer: Yellowing leaves that wilt during the day and internal stem browning indicate Fusarium wilt (Fusarium oxysporum). Once a plant shows symptoms, it cannot be saved. (1) Uproot and burn the affected plant with its root ball — do NOT compost. (2) Drench the planting hole with Trichoderma viride (10 g/L) + lime (50 g/hole). (3) Do NOT plant susceptible crops in that spot for 3-4 years — rotate with maize or rice. (4) Solarize the soil during the hottest months. (5) Use resistant varieties (FHIA series for banana). (6) Always use tissue-culture plantlets or certified disease-free suckers for new plantings — the fungus persists in infected planting material.
