question: Misawa. tomato mara nyalo yado gi kuodo ma rateng'. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Dark spots on leaves with white fungal growth on the underside and rotting fruit indicate late blight (Phytophthora infestans). This disease can destroy a field within DAYS in wet weather. (1) Spray mancozeb (2.5 g/L) OR metalaxyl-M + mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) at 2 g/L, alternating every 7 days. (2) Improve staking and pruning so leaves don't touch soil. (3) NEVER work in the field when leaves are wet. (4) Remove and bury infected plant material away from the field. (5) Plant resistant varieties like Rio Grande or Roma VF. (6) Apply mulch to reduce rain splash. Pre-harvest interval for mancozeb: 5 days.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Misawa. rice mara nigi kute matindo e oboke. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Holes in stems and 'dead hearts' (withered central shoot) indicate stem borers (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus). (1) Pull out and destroy dead heart plants — larvae inside can spread to healthy plants. (2) Apply crushed neem leaves (1 kg/10 L water, steep 24 hours) into the leaf whorl — repeat weekly. question: Misawa. cowpea mara nyalo yado gi kuodo ma rateng'. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: White powdery coating on leaves indicates powdery mildew (Erysiphales). It reduces photosynthesis and weakens plants. (1) Spray sulfur-based fungicide (micronized sulfur at 3 g/L) or potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) every 7 days. (2) Improve air circulation by wider spacing and removing excess foliage. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation — water at the base of plants. (4) Spray a solution of 1 part milk to 9 parts water — milk proteins have antifungal properties effective against powdery mildew. Apply weekly. (5) Remove and burn heavily infected leaves. Pre-harvest interval for sulfur: 1 day.
source: ICIPE Integrated Pest Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Misawa. mango mara nigi kute matindo e oboke. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Soft spots on fruit with small puncture marks and larvae (maggots) inside indicate fruit fly (Bactrocera / Ceratitis spp.). (1) Collect ALL fallen and infested fruit daily — place them in a sealed black plastic bag and leave in the sun for 7 days to kill larvae. (2) Use methyl eugenol pheromone traps (1 trap per 0.1 ha). (3) Apply GF-120 (Spinosad-based fruit fly bait) as spot sprays on a small patch of leaves — do NOT spray the fruit. (4) Bag individual fruits with paper bags when they reach half-size. (5) Plough the soil under the tree canopy to expose pupae. (6) NEVER use unapproved systemic insecticides on fruit crops.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Misawa. groundnut mara ok dongo maber, oboke towo. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near groundnut to attract them. (5) If infestation is severe and ants are present (ants farm aphids), apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. Remove ants with a sticky barrier around plant stems first.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Misawa. yam mara nyalo yado gi kuodo ma rateng'. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: The yellow-green leaf pattern you describe is Cassava Mosaic Disease caused by geminiviruses transmitted by whiteflies. There is no chemical cure. (1) Uproot and burn ALL affected plants immediately — do NOT use them as planting material. (2) Use certified mosaic-resistant varieties: TME 419, TMS 30572, or IITA-TMS-I011412. (3) Plant stakes at the recommended spacing of 1 m × 1 m. (4) Avoid recycling stakes from infected fields. (5) Intercrop with maize or cowpea to reduce whitefly populations. Contact your nearest IITA or NRCRI extension office for free resistant planting material.

question: Misawa. cocoa mara nigi kute matindo e oboke. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Swollen stems and reduced pod production indicate Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus (CSSV) transmitted by mealybugs. There is NO cure. (1) Cut down the infected tree and all trees within a 5-meter radius — the virus spreads underground through root grafts. (2) Burn all felled material on site. (3) Leave the land fallow for at least one year before replanting. (4) Plant CSSV-tolerant hybrids (e.g., CRIN series from Nigeria). (5) Control the mealybug vector by banding tree trunks with chlorpyrifos-treated bands. (6) Contact CRIN or the Cocoa Research Institute for replanting support and certified material.

question: Misawa. plantain mara nigi kute matindo e oboke. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Dark brown streaks that enlarge to black spots on leaves indicate Black Sigatoka (Mycosphaerella fijiensis). This disease can reduce yield by 50%+. (1) Remove and destroy all heavily infected leaves — do NOT leave them on the ground. (2) Spray propiconazole at 1 ml/L OR difenoconazole at 0.5 ml/L every 14-21 days during the rainy season. ALTERNATE fungicides to prevent resistance. (3) Improve drainage — standing water increases spore production. (4) Reduce planting density for better airflow (standard: 1,700 plants/ha; reduce to 1,400 if disease is severe). (5) De-leaf weekly, leaving only 8-10 functional leaves per plant.

question: Misawa. banana mara nyalo yado gi kuodo ma rateng'. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Yellowing leaves that wilt during the day and internal stem browning indicate Fusarium wilt (Fusarium oxysporum). Once a plant shows symptoms, it cannot be saved. (1) Uproot and burn the affected plant with its root ball — do NOT compost. (2) Drench the planting hole with Trichoderma viride (10 g/L) + lime (50 g/hole). (3) Do NOT plant susceptible crops in that spot for 3-4 years — rotate with maize or rice. (4) Solarize the soil during the hottest months. (5) Use resistant varieties (FHIA series for banana). (6) Always use tissue-culture plantlets or certified disease-free suckers for new plantings — the fungus persists in infected planting material.

question: Misawa. sweet potato mara nyalo yado gi kuodo ma rateng'. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Stunted growth, yellowing, swollen root galls (knots), and wilting despite moist soil indicate root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.). (1) There is no curative chemical treatment. question: Misawa. tea mara nigi kute matindo e oboke. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Reddish-brown discolouration of leaves with fine webbing indicates red spider mite (Oligonychus coffeae on tea). (1) Spray propargite at 1 ml/L OR fenazaquin at 1 ml/L ensuring thorough coverage of the underside of leaves. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L every 7 days. (3) Maintain shade — mites thrive in dry, hot, open conditions. (4) Rogue out heavily infested bushes. (5) Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides (especially synthetic pyrethroids) that kill predatory mites. Pre-plucking interval: 7 days.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Misawa. oil palm mara nigi kute matindo e oboke. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Yellowing patterns on oil palm indicate nutrient deficiency. (1) For nitrogen deficiency (uniform yellowing of older leaves): apply urea at 1-2 kg per tree per year, split into 2 applications. (2) For potassium deficiency (orange spotting on older leaves): apply muriate of potash at 2-3 kg per tree per year. (3) For magnesium deficiency (yellowing between veins of older leaves): apply kieserite at 0.5-1 kg per tree. (4) Apply empty fruit bunch (EFB) mulch at 60 t/ha around palms — it slowly releases nutrients. (5) Conduct a leaf analysis (take leaf #17 from 20 palms) to confirm which nutrients are deficient before large-scale fertiliser application.
source: KALRO Diagnostic Manual; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Misawa. amaranth mara ok dongo maber, oboke towo. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Brown spots on amaranth leaves indicate leaf spot disease (Cercospora / Alternaria spp.). (1) Remove and destroy affected leaves. (2) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR copper oxychloride at 3 g/L every 10-14 days. (3) Improve air circulation through wider spacing. (4) Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet. (5) Apply well-rotted compost at 2 t/ha to boost plant immunity. (6) Rotate with non-host crops for 2 seasons.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Misawa. cabbage mara ok dongo maber, oboke towo. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Seedlings cut at ground level overnight indicate cutworm (Agrotis spp.). (1) Hand-pick cutworms from the soil surface at night using a torch — they hide in the top 2-3 cm of soil during the day and come up to feed at night. (2) Place collars around seedlings: cut the bottom from a plastic cup or use a cardboard tube pushed 2 cm into the soil. (3) Apply neem cake at 50 g per square metre around plants — it deters egg-laying. (4) Sprinkle wood ash in a ring around each plant. (5) Plough the field 2-3 weeks before planting to expose larvae to birds.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Misawa. cashew mara nigi kute matindo e oboke. Ang'o ma nyalo timo?
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit indicate anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). (1) Remove and destroy all infected plant parts — do NOT compost them. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 10-14 days, starting at flowering. (3) Prune to improve air circulation and reduce humidity. (4) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent rain splash. (5) For the next season, use certified disease-free seed and practice 3-year crop rotation with cereals. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.

question: Sat sri akal. Meri tomato di fasal vich peele ho rahe ne te kaale dhabbe ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Fine webbing and yellow stippling on leaves indicate spider mites (Tetranychus spp.), which thrive in hot, dry conditions. question: Sat sri akal. Meri cowpea di fasal vich theek nahi vadh raha, pattiyan sukk rahiyan ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Holes in pods with frass (insect droppings) indicate pod borer (Maruca vitrata / Helicoverpa armigera). (1) Hand-pick visible caterpillars at dawn. (2) Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) at 2 g/L in the evening — it degrades in sunlight. (3) Apply neem seed kernel extract (50 g/L, soak 12 hrs, strain) weekly. (4) Plant early-maturing varieties to escape peak pest pressure. (5) Install pheromone traps (1 per 0.1 ha) to monitor moth flights. (6) After harvest, deep-plough (20-25 cm) to expose pupae to sunlight and birds. Pre-harvest interval for Bt: 0 days (safe up to harvest day).

question: Sat sri akal. Meri mango di fasal vich theek nahi vadh raha, pattiyan sukk rahiyan ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Dark bore holes on fruit and larvae inside the seed indicate mango seed weevil (Sternochetus mangiferae). The adult lays eggs on developing fruit and larvae tunnel into the seed. (1) Collect and destroy ALL fallen fruit and seeds — the weevil completes its lifecycle in the seed. (2) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L when fruit are marble-sized (2-3 cm). Repeat after 21 days. (3) Maintain orchard hygiene: remove and burn fallen leaves and debris. (4) Band tree trunks with sticky bands to trap weevils climbing up. (5) Harvest fruit slightly early (mature green stage) and store away from orchards.

question: Sat sri akal. Meri groundnut di fasal vich peele ho rahe ne te kaale dhabbe ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Soft, foul-smelling roots indicate root rot caused by soil fungi (Pythium/Phytophthora). (1) Stop watering immediately — wet soil accelerates the rot. (2) Improve drainage by creating raised beds 30 cm high. (3) Remove and destroy all affected plants. (4) Drench the remaining soil with Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg of well-rotted compost. (5) For the next planting season, solarize the soil by covering beds with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks during the hottest months. (6) Rotate groundnut with maize or sorghum for at least 2 seasons before replanting.

question: Sat sri akal. Meri banana di fasal vich peele ho rahe ne te kaale dhabbe ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Upright, crowded leaves with a 'bunchy' appearance and dark green streaking on petioles indicate Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV) transmitted by the banana aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa). question: Sat sri akal. Meri sweet potato di fasal vich peele ho rahe ne te kaale dhabbe ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Distorted, mottled leaves and stunted growth on sweet potato indicate a viral infection, often transmitted by aphids or whiteflies. question: Sat sri akal. Meri okra di fasal vich peele ho rahe ne te kaale dhabbe ne. Ki karan hai?

question: Sat sri akal. Meri millet di fasal vich pattiyan te chhote keede ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surface with grey-purple fuzz underneath indicate downy mildew (Peronospora spp.). (6) For onion, cure bulbs properly (7-10 days in sun) before storage.

question: Sat sri akal. Meri coffee di fasal vich theek nahi vadh raha, pattiyan sukk rahiyan ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on green berries that turn black and drop indicate Coffee Berry Disease (Colletotrichum kahawae). (1) Spray copper oxychloride at 5 g/L on the developing berries at 4, 8, and 12 weeks after flowering. (2) Prune to maintain an open canopy — this reduces humidity and spore dispersal. (3) Strip and burn all mummified berries remaining on branches after harvest. (4) Apply 2 t/ha of well-rotted compost to improve tree vigour. (5) Plant resistant varieties: Ruiru 11 or Batian (available in Kenya). Pre-harvest interval for copper: 21 days.
source: TNAU Agritech Portal; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sat sri akal. Meri cotton di fasal vich peele ho rahe ne te kaale dhabbe ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Angular, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown indicate bacterial blight (Xanthomonas spp.). (1) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L + streptomycin at 0.3 g/L at first sign. (2) Avoid working in the field when plants are wet — bacteria spread through water. (3) Use only acid-delinted, certified seed. (4) Rotate with maize or sorghum for 2-3 years. (5) Remove and burn all crop residues after harvest. (6) Avoid excessive nitrogen which promotes lush, susceptible growth.
source: Punjab Agricultural University Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sat sri akal. Meri tea di fasal vich peele ho rahe ne te kaale dhabbe ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Brown, necrotic spots on leaves and dieback of young shoots indicate Tea Mosquito Bug (Helopeltis spp.). (1) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L OR quinalphos at 2 ml/L, targeting the new flush. (2) Maintain adequate shade (50-60%) — open areas suffer more damage. (3) Remove alternative host plants (especially guava, cashew) near the tea field. (4) Prune affected shoots and burn them. (5) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L as a repellent. Pre-harvest interval (plucking): lambda-cyhalothrin 7 days.
source: TNAU Agritech Portal; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sat sri akal. Meri oil palm di fasal vich pattiyan te chhote keede ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Main sirf is vivaran de aadhaar te tuhadi oil palm layi pakka nidaan nahi de sakda. Vakh-vakh bimariyan ikko jahiyan dikh sakdiyan han. Kirpa karke prabhavit paudhe da namuna nede di krishi sanstha vich lai jao.

question: Sat sri akal. Meri amaranth di fasal vich theek nahi vadh raha, pattiyan sukk rahiyan ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Web-like fungal growth on leaves and stems that causes rapid wilting indicates web blight (Rhizoctonia solani). (1) Remove and destroy affected plants. (2) Spray carbendazim at 1 g/L OR propiconazole at 1 ml/L. (3) Improve field drainage and reduce planting density. (4) Apply 2 cm of organic mulch to reduce soil splash. (5) Rotate with maize or sorghum for 2 years. (6) Solarize soil before the next planting.
source: Punjab Agricultural University Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sat sri akal. Meri cabbage di fasal vich peele ho rahe ne te kaale dhabbe ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Seedlings cut at ground level overnight indicate cutworm (Agrotis spp.). (1) Hand-pick cutworms from the soil surface at night using a torch — they hide in the top 2-3 cm of soil during the day and come up to feed at night. (2) Place collars around seedlings: cut the bottom from a plastic cup or use a cardboard tube pushed 2 cm into the soil. (3) Apply neem cake at 50 g per square metre around plants — it deters egg-laying. (4) Sprinkle wood ash in a ring around each plant. (5) Plough the field 2-3 weeks before planting to expose larvae to birds.

question: Sat sri akal. Meri watermelon di fasal vich theek nahi vadh raha, pattiyan sukk rahiyan ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Yellowing leaves that wilt during the day and internal stem browning indicate Fusarium wilt (Fusarium oxysporum). Once a plant shows symptoms, it cannot be saved. (1) Uproot and burn the affected plant with its root ball — do NOT compost. (2) Drench the planting hole with Trichoderma viride (10 g/L) + lime (50 g/hole). (3) Do NOT plant susceptible crops in that spot for 3-4 years — rotate with maize or rice. (4) Solarize the soil during the hottest months. (5) Use resistant varieties (FHIA series for banana). (6) Always use tissue-culture plantlets or certified disease-free suckers for new plantings — the fungus persists in infected planting material.

question: Sat sri akal. Meri cashew di fasal vich peele ho rahe ne te kaale dhabbe ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Holes in nuts and larvae feeding inside indicate cashew weevil. (1) Collect and destroy all fallen nuts and those remaining on the tree — they harbour larvae. (2) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L when nuts are in the early development stage. (3) Maintain ground hygiene: remove leaf litter and debris under trees. (4) Band tree trunks with sticky barriers. (5) Deep-plough under tree canopies after harvest to expose pupating weevils. Pre-harvest interval: 14 days.
source: Punjab Agricultural University Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sat sri akal. Meri cassava di fasal vich pattiyan te chhote keede ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Brown leaf spots on cassava are caused by Cercospora fungi. (1) Remove severely infected lower leaves and burn them. (2) Spray mancozeb (2 g/L of water) or copper oxychloride (3 g/L) every 10-14 days during wet weather. (3) Improve air circulation by widening plant spacing to 1 m × 1 m. (4) Apply mulch to prevent rain splash that spreads spores. (5) For the next crop, choose a well-drained field and apply 2 t/ha of well-rotted compost to strengthen plant resistance. Fungicide pre-harvest interval: minimum 21 days.
source: Punjab Agricultural University Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sat sri akal. Meri cowpea di fasal vich pattiyan te chhote keede ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Stunted growth, yellowing, swollen root galls (knots), and wilting despite moist soil indicate root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.). (1) There is no curative chemical treatment. (2) Incorporate fresh neem leaves or neem cake at 500 kg/ha into the soil 2 weeks before the next planting. (3) Solarize the soil with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks. (4) Plant marigold (Tagetes erecta) as a trap crop — its roots release natural nematicides. (5) Rotate with maize, sorghum, or millet for 2-3 seasons — these are non-hosts. (6) Apply well-composted manure at 5 t/ha; the microbial activity suppresses nematodes.
source: Punjab Agricultural University Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sat sri akal. Meri mango di fasal vich pattiyan te chhote keede ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Dark bore holes on fruit and larvae inside the seed indicate mango seed weevil (Sternochetus mangiferae). The adult lays eggs on developing fruit and larvae tunnel into the seed. (1) Collect and destroy ALL fallen fruit and seeds — the weevil completes its lifecycle in the seed. (2) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L when fruit are marble-sized (2-3 cm). Repeat after 21 days. (3) Maintain orchard hygiene: remove and burn fallen leaves and debris. (4) Band tree trunks with sticky bands to trap weevils climbing up. (5) Harvest fruit slightly early (mature green stage) and store away from orchards.
source: ICAR Crop Production Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sat sri akal. Meri groundnut di fasal vich pattiyan te chhote keede ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Brown spots on groundnut leaves indicate leaf spot disease (Cercospora / Alternaria spp.). (1) Remove and destroy affected leaves. (2) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR copper oxychloride at 3 g/L every 10-14 days. (3) Improve air circulation through wider spacing. (4) Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet. (5) Apply well-rotted compost at 2 t/ha to boost plant immunity. (6) Rotate with non-host crops for 2 seasons.
source: Punjab Agricultural University Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sat sri akal. Meri yam di fasal vich peele ho rahe ne te kaale dhabbe ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Soft, watery rot of tubers during storage indicates tuber rot caused by fungi or bacteria. (1) Sort tubers carefully DURING harvest — any cut, bruised, or insect-damaged tuber must be consumed immediately or processed, not stored. (2) Cure tubers by spreading them in a well-ventilated shaded area for 2-3 days, then dust cut surfaces with wood ash. (3) Store in a cool, dry, ventilated place — yam barns with vertical stacking work well. (4) Never store in sealed plastic bags — they trap moisture. (5) Inspect stored tubers weekly and remove any showing signs of rot. (6) For loose tubers, dust with Trichoderma powder (2 g per tuber) before storage.
source: Punjab Agricultural University Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sat sri akal. Meri cocoa di fasal vich theek nahi vadh raha, pattiyan sukk rahiyan ne. Ki karan hai?
answer: Dense clusters of small, distorted shoots ('witches' brooms') indicate Witches' Broom Disease caused by Moniliophthora perniciosa. (1) Prune and burn ALL brooms and infected branches — cut at least 15 cm BELOW the visible broom into healthy wood. (2) Remove diseased pods. (3) Apply copper oxychloride at 3 g/L during flowering to protect new pods. (4) Maintain 40-50% shade — full sun exposure stresses trees and increases susceptibility. (5) Plant resistant cultivars where available (e.g., TSH series). (6) Disinfect pruning tools with 10% bleach solution between trees.
source: TNAU Agritech Portal; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Vanakkam. En plantain nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Dark brown streaks that enlarge to black spots on leaves indicate Black Sigatoka (Mycosphaerella fijiensis). This disease can reduce yield by 50%+. (1) Remove and destroy all heavily infected leaves — do NOT leave them on the ground. (2) Spray propiconazole at 1 ml/L OR difenoconazole at 0.5 ml/L every 14-21 days during the rainy season. ALTERNATE fungicides to prevent resistance. (3) Improve drainage — standing water increases spore production. (4) Reduce planting density for better airflow (standard: 1,700 plants/ha; reduce to 1,400 if disease is severe). (5) De-leaf weekly, leaving only 8-10 functional leaves per plant.

question: Vanakkam. En sorghum nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Discoloured, mouldy grain heads indicate grain mold caused by a complex of fungi (Fusarium, Curvularia, Alternaria). (1) Harvest at the RIGHT maturity — delayed harvest increases mold. Grain should be hard and not produce milky liquid when pressed. (2) Dry grains immediately to 12-13% moisture. Use raised drying racks. (3) Sort and discard all discoloured grains before storage. (4) Store in hermetic (PICS) bags or clean metal containers. (5) For the next season, plant mold-tolerant varieties (e.g., ICSV series for sorghum). (6) NEVER consume or feed visibly mouldy grain — it may contain mycotoxins.

question: Vanakkam. En sweet potato nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Tunnels in tubers with a bitter taste and smell indicate sweet potato weevil (Cylas spp.). (1) Hill up (mound) soil around the base of plants to cover exposed roots — weevils enter through soil cracks. (2) Remove and destroy all infested tubers and debris after harvest. (3) Rotate land — do NOT plant sweet potato in the same field for 2 years. (4) Apply neem cake at 200 kg/ha at planting. (5) Irrigate regularly to prevent soil cracking. (6) Use early-maturing varieties (3-4 months) and harvest immediately at maturity — delayed harvest increases weevil damage.

question: Vanakkam. En onion manjallaga maaruthu, karuppu pulligaludan. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Purple-brown oval lesions on leaves and flower stalks indicate purple blotch (Alternaria porri). (1) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR iprodione at 1.5 g/L every 10 days. (2) Avoid excessive nitrogen — apply NPK 10-10-20 rather than high-nitrogen fertilisers. (3) Ensure good field drainage. (4) Rotate with non-allium crops for 3 years. (5) Harvest bulbs only when necks are fully dry; cure properly before storage. Pre-harvest interval: mancozeb 7 days.
source: TNAU Agritech Portal; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Vanakkam. En pepper ilaigalil chinna poochigal ullana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Brown spots on pepper leaves indicate leaf spot disease (Cercospora / Alternaria spp.). (1) Remove and destroy affected leaves. (2) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR copper oxychloride at 3 g/L every 10-14 days. (3) Improve air circulation through wider spacing. (4) Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet. (5) Apply well-rotted compost at 2 t/ha to boost plant immunity. (6) Rotate with non-host crops for 2 seasons.

question: Vanakkam. En okra nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: White powdery coating on leaves indicates powdery mildew (Erysiphales). It reduces photosynthesis and weakens plants. (1) Spray sulfur-based fungicide (micronized sulfur at 3 g/L) or potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) every 7 days. (2) Improve air circulation by wider spacing and removing excess foliage. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation — water at the base of plants. (4) Spray a solution of 1 part milk to 9 parts water — milk proteins have antifungal properties effective against powdery mildew. Apply weekly. (5) Remove and burn heavily infected leaves. Pre-harvest interval for sulfur: 1 day.

question: Vanakkam. En millet ilaigalil chinna poochigal ullana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Damaged grain heads with small holes and frass indicate head miner / head bug (various species). (1) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L at 50% flowering and repeat after 10 days. (2) Plant early and uniformly to synchronize flowering. (3) Use pheromone traps to time sprays. (4) Remove alternative grass hosts from field borders. (5) Apply neem seed kernel extract (50 g/L) if synthetic insecticides are unavailable. Pre-harvest interval: lambda-cyhalothrin 14 days.
source: Punjab Agricultural University Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Vanakkam. En coffee nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Soft, foul-smelling roots indicate root rot caused by soil fungi (Pythium/Phytophthora). (1) Stop watering immediately — wet soil accelerates the rot. (2) Improve drainage by creating raised beds 30 cm high. (3) Remove and destroy all affected plants. (4) Drench the remaining soil with Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg of well-rotted compost. (5) For the next planting season, solarize the soil by covering beds with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks during the hottest months. (6) Rotate coffee with maize or sorghum for at least 2 seasons before replanting.

question: Vanakkam. En watermelon manjallaga maaruthu, karuppu pulligaludan. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near watermelon to attract them. (5) If infestation is severe and ants are present (ants farm aphids), apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. Remove ants with a sticky barrier around plant stems first.

question: Vanakkam. En cashew nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit indicate anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). (1) Remove and destroy all infected plant parts — do NOT compost them. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 10-14 days, starting at flowering. (3) Prune to improve air circulation and reduce humidity. (4) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent rain splash. (5) For the next season, use certified disease-free seed and practice 3-year crop rotation with cereals. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.

question: Vanakkam. En cassava manjallaga maaruthu, karuppu pulligaludan. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: The yellow-green leaf pattern you describe is Cassava Mosaic Disease caused by geminiviruses transmitted by whiteflies. There is no chemical cure. (1) Uproot and burn ALL affected plants immediately — do NOT use them as planting material. (2) Use certified mosaic-resistant varieties: TME 419, TMS 30572, or IITA-TMS-I011412. (3) Plant stakes at the recommended spacing of 1 m × 1 m. (4) Avoid recycling stakes from infected fields. (5) Intercrop with maize or cowpea to reduce whitefly populations. Contact your nearest IITA or NRCRI extension office for free resistant planting material.
source: ICAR Crop Production Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Vanakkam. En maize ilaigalil chinna poochigal ullana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Chlorotic streaks following leaf veins indicate Maize Streak Virus transmitted by leafhoppers (Cicadulina spp.). There is no cure. (1) Remove and destroy all affected plants immediately. (2) Plant early at the onset of rains to avoid peak leafhopper populations. (3) Use streak-resistant hybrids: ZM 623, SC 627, or WH 505. (4) Do not plant maize near irrigated vegetable fields, which harbor leafhoppers year-round. (5) Apply carbofuran granules at 1.5 kg a.i./ha to the soil at planting to control early-season vectors. (6) Save seed only from completely disease-free plants.

question: Vanakkam. En tomato manjallaga maaruthu, karuppu pulligaludan. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Fine webbing and yellow stippling on leaves indicate spider mites (Tetranychus spp.), which thrive in hot, dry conditions. (1) Spray the underside of leaves with a strong jet of water every 3 days to dislodge mites and break webbing. (2) Apply micronized sulfur at 3 g/L or abamectin at 0.5 ml/L. (3) Avoid pyrethroids and broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill predatory mites and trigger mite explosions. (4) Increase humidity around plants by mulching and watering the ground (not leaves) in the morning. (5) For heavy infestation, release Phytoseiulus persimilis predatory mites — 10/m².

question: Vanakkam. En rice nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Bronze-orange discolouration of older leaves ("bronzing") indicates iron toxicity, common in waterlogged, acidic soils. (1) Drain the field for 3-5 days to aerate the soil — this allows iron to precipitate out of the soil solution. (2) Apply lime (2-4 t/ha) to raise soil pH above 5.0. (3) Use NPK 15-15-15 fertiliser rather than single-nutrient fertilisers — potassium helps reduce iron uptake. (4) Plant tolerant varieties: NERICA-L series or TOX 4004. (5) In the next season, avoid continuous flooding of young seedlings; use alternate wetting and drying irrigation.

question: Vanakkam. En yam nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Holes in leaves and tubers indicate yam beetle (Heteroligus spp.). (1) Hand-pick beetles at night when they are active and visible with a torch. (4) Hill up (re-mound) yam mounds to expose beetles and their eggs. (5) Plant resistant varieties: Dioscorea rotundata cultivars show better tolerance. (6) After harvest, deep-plough to expose overwintering beetles to predators.

source: Punjab Agricultural University Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Vanakkam. En sorghum manjallaga maaruthu, karuppu pulligaludan. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Holes in stems and 'dead hearts' (withered central shoot) indicate stem borers (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus). (1) Pull out and destroy dead heart plants — larvae inside can spread to healthy plants. (2) Apply crushed neem leaves (1 kg/10 L water, steep 24 hours) into the leaf whorl — repeat weekly. (3) Apply carbofuran 3G granules at 0.75 kg a.i./ha into the whorl at knee-height stage. (4) After harvest, cut stubble to ground level and bury or burn crop residues to kill overwintering larvae. (5) Rotate with legumes (cowpea, groundnut) to break the pest cycle.
source: TNAU Agritech Portal; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Vanakkam. En banana nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Upright, crowded leaves with a 'bunchy' appearance and dark green streaking on petioles indicate Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV) transmitted by the banana aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa). There is NO cure. (1) Uproot and destroy the entire plant including the corm — bury or burn it. (2) Control the aphid vector by spraying imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L on all surrounding plants. (3) Never use suckers from an affected field for new plantings. (4) Use tissue-culture plantlets — they are guaranteed virus-free. (5) Contact your agricultural extension office to report BBTV — it is a notifiable disease in most countries. (6) Quarantine any new planting material for 4 weeks.
source: ICAR Crop Production Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Vanakkam. En onion nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surface with grey-purple fuzz underneath indicate downy mildew (Peronospora spp.). (1) Spray metalaxyl-M + mancozeb at 2 g/L OR phosphorous acid at 3 ml/L every 7-10 days. (2) Improve field drainage and air circulation. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening — water early morning instead. (4) Remove crop debris after harvest. (5) Use disease-free seed for the next planting. (6) For onion, cure bulbs properly (7-10 days in sun) before storage.
source: ICAR Crop Production Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Vanakkam. En pepper nandraga valaramal, ilaigal kayalagindrana. Enna seiya vendum?
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near pepper to attract them. (5) If infestation is severe and ants are present (ants farm aphids), apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. Remove ants with a sticky barrier around plant stems first.
source: ICAR Crop Production Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye coffee behele beKutatochache lay tiNish tiNish teSarochi alubachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Soft, foul-smelling roots indicate root rot caused by soil fungi (Pythium/Phytophthora). (1) Stop watering immediately — wet soil accelerates the rot. (2) Improve drainage by creating raised beds 30 cm high. (3) Remove and destroy all affected plants. (4) Drench the remaining soil with Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg of well-rotted compost. (5) For the next planting season, solarize the soil by covering beds with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks during the hottest months. (6) Rotate coffee with maize or sorghum for at least 2 seasons before replanting.
source: EIAR Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye cotton behele beKutatochache lay tiNish tiNish teSarochi alubachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Yellowing leaf margins that curl downward ('hopper burn') indicate jassids (Amrasca biguttula). (1) Spray imidacloprid at 0.3 ml/L OR acetamiprid at 0.2 g/L. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L as a repellent. (3) Maintain adequate soil moisture — drought-stressed crops are more attractive to jassids. (4) Use yellow sticky traps (1 per 2 m²). (5) Plant resistant varieties with hairy leaves (hirsutum-type cotton). Pre-harvest interval for imidacloprid: 21 days.
source: ATA Agricultural Transformation Agency Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye tea behele bdamena alebado newa, keTafochache derashochi nachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Brown, necrotic spots on leaves and dieback of young shoots indicate Tea Mosquito Bug (Helopeltis spp.). (1) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L OR quinalphos at 2 ml/L, targeting the new flush. (2) Maintain adequate shade (50-60%) — open areas suffer more damage. (3) Remove alternative host plants (especially guava, cashew) near the tea field. (4) Prune affected shoots and burn them. (5) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L as a repellent. Pre-harvest interval (plucking): lambda-cyhalothrin 7 days.
source: ATA Agricultural Transformation Agency Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye oil palm behele bdamena alebado newa, keTafochache derashochi nachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Brown spots on oil palm leaves indicate leaf spot disease (Cercospora / Alternaria spp.). (1) Remove and destroy affected leaves. (2) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR copper oxychloride at 3 g/L every 10-14 days. (3) Improve air circulation through wider spacing. (4) Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet. (5) Apply well-rotted compost at 2 t/ha to boost plant immunity. (6) Rotate with non-host crops for 2 seasons.
source: ICRISAT Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye amaranth behele bdamena alebado newa, keTafochache derashochi nachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Web-like fungal growth on leaves and stems that causes rapid wilting indicates web blight (Rhizoctonia solani). (1) Remove and destroy affected plants. (2) Spray carbendazim at 1 g/L OR propiconazole at 1 ml/L. (3) Improve field drainage and reduce planting density. (4) Apply 2 cm of organic mulch to reduce soil splash. (5) Rotate with maize or sorghum for 2 years. (6) Solarize soil before the next planting.
source: ATA Agricultural Transformation Agency Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye cabbage behele bdamena alebado newa, keTafochache derashochi nachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Small holes in leaves and green caterpillars that wriggle violently when disturbed indicate diamondback moth (Plutella xylostella). (1) Spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki) at 2 g/L every 7 days — it targets caterpillars only. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (3) Use pheromone traps to monitor moth populations. (4) Rotate insecticide groups — diamondback moth rapidly develops resistance. Alternate Bt with spinosad at 0.3 ml/L. (5) Remove and destroy crop residues after harvest. (6) Plant trap crop: Indian mustard attracts moths away from cabbage.
source: ICRISAT Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye watermelon behele beKutatochache lay tiNish tiNish teSarochi alubachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Soft spots on fruit with small puncture marks and larvae (maggots) inside indicate fruit fly (Bactrocera / Ceratitis spp.). (1) Collect ALL fallen and infested fruit daily — place them in a sealed black plastic bag and leave in the sun for 7 days to kill larvae. (2) Use methyl eugenol pheromone traps (1 trap per 0.1 ha). (3) Apply GF-120 (Spinosad-based fruit fly bait) as spot sprays on a small patch of leaves — do NOT spray the fruit. (4) Bag individual fruits with paper bags when they reach half-size. (5) Plough the soil under the tree canopy to expose pupae. (6) NEVER use unapproved systemic insecticides on fruit crops.
source: EIAR Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye cassava behele bdamena alebado newa, keTafochache derashochi nachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Green mites (Mononychellus tanajoa) cause stippling and leaf distortion on cassava. (1) Spray water forcefully on the underside of leaves to dislodge mites. (2) Apply sulfur-based miticide at 2 g/L, or micronized sulfur dust at 15 kg/ha during dry weather. (3) Avoid pyrethroid insecticides — they kill predatory mites that control this pest. (4) Maintain plant health with adequate potassium fertiliser (apply muriate of potash at 60 kg/ha). (5) Introduce Typhlodromalus aripo predatory mites available from IITA if the problem recurs across multiple seasons.
source: ATA Agricultural Transformation Agency Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye maize behele beKutatochache lay tiNish tiNish teSarochi alubachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Yellowing of lower leaves (starting at the tip and moving inward in a V shape on maize) indicates nitrogen deficiency. (1) Apply urea (46-0-0) at the rate of 50 kg/ha — split into two doses: half at 3 weeks after planting, half at 6 weeks. Place fertiliser in a band 5 cm from the plant and 3 cm deep — do NOT leave it on the soil surface. (2) Alternatively, apply well-composted poultry manure at 5 t/ha. (3) Intercrop with cowpea or groundnut — they fix atmospheric nitrogen into the soil for your maize. (4) Do NOT apply urea when the soil is dry; wait until after rainfall or irrigate lightly.
source: EIAR Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye tomato behele bicha teterawochi keTikur leKawochi gar. Minder adergale?
answer: Winding tunnels (mines) inside leaves indicate leaf miner (Tuta absoluta / Liriomyza spp.). (1) Remove and destroy mined leaves immediately — each leaf may contain 3-5 larvae. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L with a few drops of liquid soap as a sticker, every 5-7 days. (3) Use pheromone traps (Delta traps with Tuta lure) at 20 traps/ha. (4) Apply spinosad at 0.3 ml/L if infestation exceeds 5% of leaves. (5) Remove all crop debris after harvest and solarize the soil. (6) For greenhouse crops, use insect-proof (50-mesh) netting.
source: ICRISAT Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye rice behele beKutatochache lay tiNish tiNish teSarochi alubachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Grey-whitish lesions on leaves with brown borders indicate rice blast (Magnaporthe grisea). This is the most destructive rice disease worldwide. (1) Avoid excessive nitrogen — limit urea to 60 kg/ha in blast-prone areas and split into 3 doses. (2) Spray tricyclazole at 0.6 g/L or isoprothiolane at 1 ml/L at first sign and repeat after 10-14 days. (3) Maintain 2-3 cm of standing water in the field; intermittent drying stresses plants and increases susceptibility. (4) Plant resistant varieties: NERICA 4, ARICA 3, or IR64. (5) Burn infected straw after harvest — the fungus survives in crop residue.
source: ATA Agricultural Transformation Agency Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye cowpea behele beKutatochache lay tiNish tiNish teSarochi alubachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: White powdery coating on leaves indicates powdery mildew (Erysiphales). It reduces photosynthesis and weakens plants. (1) Spray sulfur-based fungicide (micronized sulfur at 3 g/L) or potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) every 7 days. (2) Improve air circulation by wider spacing and removing excess foliage. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation — water at the base of plants. (4) Spray a solution of 1 part milk to 9 parts water — milk proteins have antifungal properties effective against powdery mildew. Apply weekly. (5) Remove and burn heavily infected leaves. Pre-harvest interval for sulfur: 1 day.
source: EIAR Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye groundnut behele beKutatochache lay tiNish tiNish teSarochi alubachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Orange-brown powdery pustules on leaves indicate rust (Puccinia spp.). (1) Spray propiconazole at 1 ml/L OR tebuconazole at 0.5 ml/L at first sign. (2) Plant resistant varieties where available. (3) Avoid excessive nitrogen — it promotes lush, susceptible growth. (4) Remove and destroy crop residues after harvest. (5) Practice early planting to avoid peak rust season. (6) Apply balanced NPK (not just urea) to strengthen cell walls.

question: Selam. Ye yam behele bicha teterawochi keTikur leKawochi gar. Minder adergale?
answer: Holes in leaves and tubers indicate yam beetle (Heteroligus spp.). (1) Hand-pick beetles at night when they are active and visible with a torch. (2) Apply carbofuran granules at 1.0 kg a.i./ha to the soil around the mounds at planting. (3) Delay planting until after the first heavy rains when beetle populations naturally decline. (4) Hill up (re-mound) yam mounds to expose beetles and their eggs. (5) Plant resistant varieties: Dioscorea rotundata cultivars show better tolerance. (6) After harvest, deep-plough to expose overwintering beetles to predators.
source: ATA Agricultural Transformation Agency Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye cocoa behele beKutatochache lay tiNish tiNish teSarochi alubachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Holes in pods with frass (insect droppings) indicate pod borer (Maruca vitrata / Helicoverpa armigera). (1) Hand-pick visible caterpillars at dawn. (2) Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) at 2 g/L in the evening — it degrades in sunlight. (3) Apply neem seed kernel extract (50 g/L, soak 12 hrs, strain) weekly. (4) Plant early-maturing varieties to escape peak pest pressure. (5) Install pheromone traps (1 per 0.1 ha) to monitor moth flights. (6) After harvest, deep-plough (20-25 cm) to expose pupae to sunlight and birds. Pre-harvest interval for Bt: 0 days (safe up to harvest day).
source: ICRISAT Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye sorghum behele bicha teterawochi keTikur leKawochi gar. Minder adergale?
answer: Discoloured, mouldy grain heads indicate grain mold caused by a complex of fungi (Fusarium, Curvularia, Alternaria). (1) Harvest at the RIGHT maturity — delayed harvest increases mold. Grain should be hard and not produce milky liquid when pressed. (2) Dry grains immediately to 12-13% moisture. Use raised drying racks. (3) Sort and discard all discoloured grains before storage. (4) Store in hermetic (PICS) bags or clean metal containers. (5) For the next season, plant mold-tolerant varieties (e.g., ICSV series for sorghum). (6) NEVER consume or feed visibly mouldy grain — it may contain mycotoxins.
source: EIAR Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye banana behele bdamena alebado newa, keTafochache derashochi nachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Stunted growth, yellowing, swollen root galls (knots), and wilting despite moist soil indicate root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.). (1) There is no curative chemical treatment. (2) Incorporate fresh neem leaves or neem cake at 500 kg/ha into the soil 2 weeks before the next planting. (3) Solarize the soil with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks. (4) Plant marigold (Tagetes erecta) as a trap crop — its roots release natural nematicides. (5) Rotate with maize, sorghum, or millet for 2-3 seasons — these are non-hosts. (6) Apply well-composted manure at 5 t/ha; the microbial activity suppresses nematodes.
source: ATA Agricultural Transformation Agency Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye onion behele bdamena alebado newa, keTafochache derashochi nachewi. Minder adergale?
answer: Silvery streaks on leaves and distorted young growth indicate thrips. (1) Spray spinosad at 0.3 ml/L or neem oil at 5 ml/L every 5 days. (2) Use blue sticky traps (thrips are more attracted to blue than yellow), 1 trap per 5 m². (3) Remove weeds from around the field — they serve as alternative hosts. (4) Maintain adequate soil moisture — drought stressed plants are more vulnerable. (5) For heavy infestations, apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L as a soil drench. Pre-harvest interval: spinosad 3 days.
source: ATA Agricultural Transformation Agency Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Selam. Ye pepper behele bicha teterawochi keTikur leKawochi gar. Minder adergale?
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit indicate anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). (1) Remove and destroy all infected plant parts — do NOT compost them. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 10-14 days, starting at flowering. (3) Prune to improve air circulation and reduce humidity. (4) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent rain splash. (5) For the next season, use certified disease-free seed and practice 3-year crop rotation with cereals. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.

question: Selam. Ye oil palm behele bicha teterawochi keTikur leKawochi gar. Minder adergale?
answer: Yellowing patterns on oil palm indicate nutrient deficiency. (1) For nitrogen deficiency (uniform yellowing of older leaves): apply urea at 1-2 kg per tree per year, split into 2 applications. (2) For potassium deficiency (orange spotting on older leaves): apply muriate of potash at 2-3 kg per tree per year. (3) For magnesium deficiency (yellowing between veins of older leaves): apply kieserite at 0.5-1 kg per tree. (4) Apply empty fruit bunch (EFB) mulch at 60 t/ha around palms — it slowly releases nutrients. (5) Conduct a leaf analysis (take leaf #17 from 20 palms) to confirm which nutrients are deficient before large-scale fertiliser application.
source: ICRISAT Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Kod bende mar oduma osechako ketho cham mara mar bando. Ang'o manyalo konya?
answer: Kod bende mar oduma (fall armyworm) nyalo ketho cham mokalo mana moromo 50% ka ok ochungi. Moko mag gik mitim: (1) Non anena magi pile ka iyudo kata nyath kod achiel kende to itim gik ma dwarore. (2) Neem pesticide mowinjore ma nitie e sirkal — dhi ir ofisa mar kilimo ma ing'iyo kaka inyalo tiyo kode. (3) Puodho man kod yath moromo malo nyalo konyo chungo kod moko ma ok keth ahinya. (4) Puodh cham kinyoro e kinde ma ok rom gi chieng' moduogo kod bende e kinde ma olokore kod puodho mamoko. Kuom kony mo medore, dhi ir ofisa mar kilimo man machiegni.
source: FAO Fall Armyworm Management Guide; KALRO extension bulletin

question: Cham mara mar bando onyiso rangi ma rachar e it. Ne atiyo gi manyien to pok okonya.
answer: Rangi ma rachar e it cham mar bando inyalo bedo gi gima omiyo mang'eny — nyalo bedo tuo mar phosphorus, kata tuo mar nitrogen, kata chandruok mar tiende. Ka ne itiyo gi manyien (DAP) to pod itieko gi tuo, nyalo bedo ni lowo ok oyiego maber. Tim magi: (1) Kel sampul mar lowo ir ofisa mar kilimo mondo gine ane gima remo. (2) Kuom lowo ma ok winj manyien maber, nyiso ni pH ok rom — liming nyalo konyo. (3) Ne ane ka nitie tuo mar virus ma golo rangi e it. Kik ikaw okang' moro amora kapok ing'eyo gima chando chameno — nyalo bedo ni iweyo pesa.
source: KALRO Soil Fertility Guide; IPNI Nutrient Deficiency Identification

question: Toke mara mag muogo otudore, to ka achamo to nitie thuolo matindo matindo e iye. Bende yath ok dong' malo.
answer: Gima inyiso chalre gi tuo ma iluongo ni cassava mosaic disease (CMD) kata cassava brown streak disease (CBSD). Magi gin tuo ma kelo nyakowuok mang'eny e puothe man Nyansa. Tim magi: (1) Puth toke moko duto ma ondiki gi tuo — wiyo kanyachiel. (2) Kaw toke manyien koa kuom miech sirkal kata KALRO — tim nyono ni gin toke ma ok nyal mako tuo (CMD-resistant: TME 419, MM96/5280). (3) Kik ipidh toke moa kuom puodho ma tuo osemako. (4) Puodho man gi yath mang'eny nyalo konyo geng'o lando tuo. Dhi ir ofisa mar kilimo e alworani.
source: IITA Cassava Disease Management; KALRO Cassava Best Practices

question: Muogo mara ka achamo to tek, to bende osebedo gi rangi ma rachar e iye. Nyaka arom kapok otimo kare?
answer: Muogo ma tek kod rangi ma rachar e iye nyiso ni kama oseng'iewo mokwongo. Moko mag gik mitim: (1) Ywar muogo ka podi tin — ka osebedo e lowo kuom dwe mang'eny, chame tek. Maduong' mar muogo mitimo kare en dwe 8-12 bang' pitho. (2) Kuom muogo ma osekethore, inyalo ywayo kendo loso gik moko kaka flour kata chips e od tong'. (3) Puodho ma nitie pi mang'eny nyalo miyo muogo medo bet gi tuo moloyo. Los sulu mag pi oko e puodho. (4) Kuom seche mabiro, pidh muogo e ndara (mounds) mondo kik obet e pi mang'eny.
source: KALRO Cassava Harvest & Post-Harvest Guide; FAO Root & Tuber Bulletin

question: Bel mara oserwako kothe kendo wigi otwo ka podi tin. Yamo bende otucho moko piny.
answer: Kothe mar bel ma gi two kata ma wigi otwo nyiso ni nitie tuo kata chandruok mar pi. Moko mag gik mitim: (1) Ne ane ka nitie tuo mar ergot kata grain mold — magi gin tuo ma landore e kinde mag koth. (2) Ka pi oromo e puodho, los sulu mag pi. (3) Keyo bel ka ochiek maber — kik iwe e puodho kuom kinde malach. (4) Riambo bel e chieng' kata e ober (dryer) ma piny oyudo yamo maber. (5) Kan bel e kar ma otwo, ma yamo donjoe, to ma okinyal donjoe gi olenge. Iromo penjo ofisa mar kilimo mondo okonyi gi kit bel ma ok mak tuo ahinya.
source: KALRO Sorghum Production Guide; ICRISAT Post-Harvest Management

question: Bel mara ochako nigi ondiegi matindo ma rachar e it kod e tiend kothe. Be inyalo konya?
answer: Wachno chalre gi tuo ma iluongo ni sorghum midge (Stenodiplosis sorghicola) kata aphids. Ondiegi matindo ma ochung' e tiend kothe nyalo ketho cham mokalo 30%. Tim magi: (1) Non ane ka ondiegi nitie mang'eny — ka wan'gi mang'eny to itim gima dwarore. (2) Pidh bel e ndalo ma kik rom gi chieng' moduogo mag ondiegigo. (3) Kuom bel manyien, nyis ni nitie kit bel ma ok mak ondiegigo ka Seredo kata Gadam. (4) Ka ondiegi ng'eny ahinya, tim nyono gi pesticide ma ofisa mar kilimo osenyiso — kik ing'iew moro amora ma ok g'oyiego. Dhi ir ofisa mar kilimo e alworani.
source: ICRISAT Sorghum Pest Guide; KALRO Pest Advisory

question: Nyanyondo mara otucho ma kik ochopo piny. A tuche gode, to nitie ma otwo e yath.
answer: Nyanyondo ma otucho ka podi tin kata ma otwo e yath nyiso ni nitie chandruok. Moko mag gik mitim: (1) Ne ane ka nitie tuo mar blossom-end rot — ma en tuo moa kuom calcium ma oromo. (2) Mul manyien (mulching) nyalo konyo rito pi e lowo. (3) Pi ma oromo jogi pile — kik iwe lowo otwo chuth. (4) Ne ane ka nitie tuo mar early blight kata late blight — magi nyalo miyo nyanyondo tucho. (5) Keyo nyanyondo ka gisechako lokore ma rachar (breaker stage) kendo iwe gichakiekie e ot — ma konyo geng'o tucho. Dhi ir ofisa mar kilimo gi sampul mar nyanyondo mosekethore.
source: KALRO Tomato Production Guide; AVRDC Tomato Disease Identification

question: Yien nyanyondo maga wiyegi olokore ma rachar, to itgi bende orachar. Nyanyondo ok dong' nyagi.
answer: Wiyegi ma rachar kod it ma rachar e yien nyanyondo chalre gi tuo mar virus kata chandruok mar lowo. Tim magi: (1) Ne ane ka nitie tuo mar tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) — ma en tuo ma whitefly lando. (2) Ka inyalo neno whitefly e it yien, tim pesticide mowinjore (neem oil kata insecticidal soap). (3) Puodho man gi yath mang'eny e bute nyalo konyo geng'o whitefly. (4) Keyo yien mosekethore chuth kendo wang'gi. (5) Kuom seche mabiro, many kit nyanyondo ma ok mak tuo ka Rio Grande, Tengeru 97, kata Tanya. Dhi ir ofisa mar kilimo.
source: AVRDC TYLCV Management; KALRO Tomato Pest Advisory

question: Oganda mara ne dongo maber to koro osechako bedo ma rachar, to itgi bende olokore. Ang'o manyalo konya?
answer: Rangi ma rachar e oganda mosebedo ka dongo maber nyiso ni gima chando inyalo bedo tuo kata chandruok mar lowo. Tim magi: (1) Rangi ma rachar e itgi nyiso ni nitie tuo mar nitrogen. Nyalo bedo ni lowo ochopo — yie mondo ofisa mar kilimo one lowoni. (2) Ne ane ka nitie tuo mar aphid kata thrips — magi nyalo golo rangi e yien. (3) Los sulu mag pi e puodho mondo pi kik chung'. (4) Oganda ok dwar pi mang'eny — pi mang'eny inyalo ketho tiende. (5) Kel sampul mar lowo gi it yath ir ofisa mar kilimo.
source: IITA Cowpea Production Guide; KALRO Legume Advisory

question: Kodhi mag oganda osebedo gi ondiegi e iye, kendo moromo ketho cham duto. Anyalo tiyo gi ang'o?
answer: Ondiegi ma chamo oganda e i keno en tuo ma luongo ni cowpea weevil (Callosobruchus maculatus). Tim magi: (1) Gol oganda oko e kar keno kendo walgi ka itieko gi yo maber — wan'o oganda mosekethore. (2) Riambo oganda e chieng' maber mondo oneg ondiegigo. (3) Kuom seche mabiro, kan oganda e airtight containers ma ondiegi ok nyal donjo e iye. (4) Iromo keto oganda e freezer kuom ndalo auchiel mondo oneg ondiegi kod tong' gik. (5) Tim nyono ni kar keno ler, otwo, to yamo donjoe maber. Iromo penjo ofisa mar kilimo kuom kit oganda machielo ma ok mak ondiegi.
source: IITA Cowpea Storage Guide; KALRO Post-Harvest Bulletin

question: Shikamoo. Mahindi yangu yana mchanga mweupe kwenye majani na hayakui vizuri. Nilitumia mbolea ya CAN lakini haikusaidia.
answer: Shikamoo. Mchanga mweupe kwenye majani ya mahindi unaweza kuwa ishara ya ukungu wa unga (powdery mildew) au upungufu wa virutubisho. Kwa kuwa ulitumia mbolea ya CAN (inayo nitrojeni), tatizo linaweza kuwa tofauti. Haya ndiyo ya kufanya: (1) Angalia kama mchanga huo unafutika ukigusa — ukiwa unafutika, ni ukungu. (2) Chukua sampuli ya mmea mzima (pamoja na mizizi) na upeleke katika ofisi ya kilimo ya kaunti au KALRO. (3) Kwa sasa, hakikisha shamba lina mifereji mizuri — ukungu hupenda unyevu. (4) Usitumie dawa yoyote kabla ya utambuzi sahihi. Ofisi ya kilimo itakusaidia bila malipo.
source: KALRO Maize Disease Guide; FAO Cereal Disease Identification

question: Mabua ya mahindi yangu yanavunjika kwa urahisi na ndani yake kuna wadudu wadogo weusi. Hii ni shida gani?
answer: Wadudu weusi ndani ya mabua ya mahindi yanayo vunjika kwa urahisi ni ishara ya stem borer (Chilo partellus). Hawa ni viwavi wanaoingia ndani ya bua na kula tishu za ndani. Haya ya kufanya: (1) Vunja mabua yote yaliyoathirika na uyachome — hii itaua viwavi waliomo. (2) Panda mahindi mapema msimu ujao kabla ya wadudu kuwa wengi. (3) Zungusha mazao — usipande mahindi kwenye shamba hilo kwa msimu mmoja; panda mikunde. (4) Aina za mahindi sugu kama H614, H6213, na KH500-33A zina uhimilivu. (5) Kama shambulizi ni kubwa, wasiliana na ofisa kilimo kuhusu dawa zinazofaa.
source: KALRO Stem Borer Management; CIMMYT Pest Guide

question: Mhogo wangu una madoa ya kahawia kwenye mizizi na ladha ni chungu. Mbegu zilitoka kwa jirani. Naweza kupanda tena?
answer: Madoa ya kahawia kwenye mizizi ya mhogo na ladha chungu ni dalili za ugonjwa wa cassava brown streak disease (CBSD). Huu ni ugonjwa hatari unaoenezwa na wadudu wadogo weupe. Haya ya kufanya: (1) USIPANDE tena vipando kutoka kwa mimea hiyo — ugonjwa unaenea kwa vipando. (2) Ng'oa mimea yote iliyoathirika na uichome. (3) Nunua vipando safi kutoka KALRO au ofisi ya kilimo — aina kama KME 08-01, Tajirika, au Kiroba ni sugu kwa CBSD. (4) USIPANDE mhogo kwenye shamba hilo kwa msimu mmoja. (5) Waelimishe majirani wako pia — ugonjwa huu unaenea kwa urahisi.
source: KALRO CBSD Management Guide; IITA Cassava Disease Advisory

question: Mihogo yangu ina mizizi midogo sana na majani yana rangi ya njano. Nimekuwa nikipanda sehemu hiyohiyo kwa miaka mitano.
answer: Mizizi midogo na majani ya njano baada ya kupanda sehemu moja kwa miaka mitano ni ishara ya uchovu wa udongo. Haya ya kufanya: (1) ACHA kupanda mhogo kwenye shamba hilo kwa misimu miwili — panda mikunde kama kunde au karanga. Mikunde inarutubisha udongo. (2) Wakati unapopanda tena mhogo, tumia mbolea ya NPK 15-15-15 kwa kiwango cha vijiko viwili kwa shina. (3) Panda kwenye matuta — si kwenye udongo tambarare. (4) Tumia vipando vipya kutoka KALRO au ofisi ya kilimo. (5) Pima udongo wako — ofisi ya kilimo inaweza kukusaidia.
source: KALRO Soil Fertility Guide; IITA Cassava Agronomy; FAO Crop Rotation Principles

question: Mpunga wangu una madoa mekundu kwenye majani na miche inanyauka. Niko Morogoro.
answer: Madoa mekundu kwenye majani ya mpunga yanayosababisha miche kunyauka ni dalili za ugonjwa wa rice blast (Magnaporthe oryzae). Huu ni ugonjwa hatari sana katika maeneo ya Morogoro. Haya ya kufanya: (1) Hakikisha shamba lina maji ya kutosha lakini si mengi — ugonjwa huu hupenda mpunga ulio na mkazo wa maji. (2) Punguza matumizi ya mbolea ya nitrojeni — nitrojeni nyingi huchochea ugonjwa. (3) Kama shambulizi limeenea zaidi ya asilimia 10, wasiliana na ofisa kilimo kuhusu dawa za ukungu. (4) Kwa msimu ujao, tumia aina sugu kama SARO 5 (TXD 306), Komboka, au Tai. (5) Usichelewe kupanda — panda mapema msimu.
source: IRRI Rice Blast Management; Kilimo Tanzania Rice Advisory; AfricaRice Technical Bulletin

question: Mchele wangu baada ya kuvuna una harufu mbaya na rangi ya kijivu. Niliuhifadhi kwenye magunia.
answer: Harufu mbaya na rangi ya kijivu kwenye mchele uliohifadhiwa ni ishara ya ukungu (mold) unaosababishwa na unyevu wakati wa uhifadhi. Haya ya kufanya: (1) USILE au kuuza mchele huo — ukungu unaweza kutoa sumu ya aflatoxin ambayo ni hatari kwa afya. (2) Kausha mchele vizuri kwenye jua kabla ya kuhifadhi — unyevu unapaswa kuwa chini ya 14%. (3) Hifadhi mchele kwenye magunia yaliyo juu ya godoro (pallets) — si chini kwenye sakafu. (4) Safisha ghala vizuri kabla ya kuhifadhi mavuno mapya. (5) Kwa msimu ujao, kausha mchele mara baada ya kuvuna — usiache kwenye shamba.
source: FAO Grain Storage Guide; Kilimo Tanzania Post-Harvest Advisory

question: Alizeti yangu ina maua madogo na mbegu nyepesi. Nilitumia mbolea ya kawaida lakini haikusaidia. Nafanya nini?
answer: Maua madogo na mbegu nyepesi kwenye alizeti yanaweza kuwa ni ishara ya upungufu wa boroni au uchavushaji hafifu. Haya ya kufanya: (1) Alizeti inahitaji boroni — upungufu wake husababisha maua madogo na mbegu tupu. Uliza ofisa kilimo kuhusu mbolea yenye boroni. (2) Hakikisha kuna nyuki wa kutosha shambani — alizeti inahitaji uchavushaji wa wadudu. Weka mizinga karibu. (3) Panda alizeti kwa nafasi — sentimita 60-75 kati ya mistari. (4) Aina kama Record, Kenya Fedha, na PAN 7352 zinafanya vizuri Tanzania.
source: Kilimo Tanzania Sunflower Guide; FAO Oilseed Advisory; ARI Naliendele Research

question: Maharage yangu yana madoa ya kahawia kwenye majani na maua yanadondoka. Hali ya hewa imekuwa na unyevu mwingi.
answer: Madoa ya kahawia na maua kudondoka kwenye maharage wakati wa unyevu mwingi ni dalili za ugonjwa wa angular leaf spot au anthracnose. Haya ya kufanya: (1) Epuka kufanya kazi shambani wakati mimea ina unyevu — magonjwa huenea kwa urahisi. (2) Ondoa na uchome majani yote yaliyoathirika. (3) Hakikisha shamba lina mifereji mizuri ya maji. (4) Kwa msimu ujao, panda aina sugu kama KK 8, KK 15, au Chelalang. (5) USITUMIE mbegu kutoka kwenye mimea iliyoathirika — nunua mbegu safi. (6) Kama shambulizi ni kubwa, wasiliana na ofisa kilimo.
source: KALRO Bean Disease Guide; CIAT Angular Leaf Spot Management

question: Viazi vitamu vyangu vina madoa meusi kwenye ngozi na ndani yake kuna michirizi myeusi. Vinauzika kweli?
answer: Madoa meusi kwenye ngozi ya viazi vitamu na michirizi myeusi ndani ni ishara ya ugonjwa wa sweet potato virus disease (SPVD) au interne cork. Haya ya kufanya: (1) Viazi vyenye michirizi myeusi havina sumu lakini ubora wake ni duni — wanunuzi watakatalia bei ya chini. Unaweza kuviuza kwa mifugo baada ya kuchemsha. (2) USIPANDE vipando kutoka kwa mimea hiyo — virusi huenea kwa vipando. (3) Nunua vipando safi kutoka KALRO — aina kama Kembu 10, Mugande, na SPK 004 ni sugu. (4) Zungusha mazao kwa misimu miwili. (5) Ondoa magugu yote shambani — magugu ni makao ya wadudu wanaoeneza virusi.
source: KALRO Sweet Potato Disease Guide; CIP Virus Management; FAO Root Crop Advisory

question: Vitunguu vyangu vinaoza kuanzia kwenye shingo na harufu ni mbaya. Nilitumia mbolea ya samadi lakini bado.
answer: Kuoza kwenye shingo la kitunguu pamoja na harufu mbaya ni dalili za ugonjwa wa neck rot (Botrytis allii) au bacterial soft rot. Haya ya kufanya: (1) Vuna vitunguu vyote mara moja vilivyo karibu kuiva — usiviache shambani. (2) Kavya (cure) vitunguu kwenye jua kwa siku 5-7 — shingo lazima likauke kabisa. (3) Kata majani BAADA ya kukausha — si kabla. (4) Hifadhi kwenye chumba chenye hewa ya kutosha, baridi, na kavu. (5) USITUMIE mbolea ya samadi ambayo haijaoza vizuri. (6) Kwa msimu ujao, zungusha mazao — usipande kitunguu sehemu hiyo kwa misimu miwili.
source: KALRO Onion Production Guide; AVRDC Onion Disease Management; FAO Onion Post-Harvest

question: Kahawa yakwa niraria nyoni nini iria njeru na ni ikunagia mawira. Kahawa ni iraruruka na ndiracanjamuka.
answer: Nyoni njeru (whiteflies) ikunagia kahawa na gutuma iraruruka ni kiritiu gitarie. Mawira maria maranyitwo ni ikunagia makoragwo na rimu na gukura ti kwega. Undu wa gwika: (1) Miti ya kahawa iraruruka niundu wa ikunagia — haragia ngano ta neem oil kana sabuni ya kiumbe. (2) Geria gwikira muti kiimbe — ikunagia itiendaga ngano iria ni igiri. (3) Menya uria mawira maria maranyitwo mari — manyitithia na moko na umatume. (4) Twika na kimenythia kiria gitari kia coffee berry disease o nginya. Thie kwa ofisa wa urimi wa gicagi kana Coffee Research Institute.
source: Coffee Research Institute Kenya; KALRO Coffee Pest Advisory

question: Ciaai ciakwa irathandukuo ni mahua maria matari mageni na ni iranyihia. Nindiraruta mathangu maria matari mega.
answer: Mahua maria matari mageni (exotic weeds) na mathangu maranyihia ni cina nyingi. Undu wa gwika: (1) Rutithania mathangu maria matari mega muno na moko — ndukanareke mahua maria mageni marahurane. (2) Hurana na mahua maria mageni maria marahota gukinyira — marahota guthutha irio cia miti. (3) Ndukanahuthire ndawa ya kuhurana na mahua utari na urutani — no ihote gukua miti ya ciai. (4) Rika handu ria ngu kana githaka kiria kihuthitwo gukuma ndawa. (5) Thie kwa ofisa wa urimi kana Tea Research Institute niguo maguuteithie.
source: Tea Research Institute Kenya; KTDA Extension; FAO Tea Cultivation

question: My coffee cherries are falling off before they ripen. Some have small holes and I see tiny insects inside. What is happening?
answer: Cherries falling prematurely with small holes and tiny insects inside is characteristic of coffee berry borer (Hypothenemus hampei). Here is what to do: (1) Pick and destroy ALL fallen cherries immediately — do not leave any on the ground. (2) Harvest ripe cherries promptly and strip all remaining cherries at end of season — no berries left on trees means no breeding ground. (3) Maintain shade at 40 to 50 percent — borer populations increase in full sun. (4) For severe infestations, contact Coffee Research Institute or county extension officer — they can advise on approved insecticides. (5) Do NOT use unregistered pesticides — coffee is an export crop and residue limits are strict.
source: Coffee Research Institute Kenya; ICIPE Coffee Berry Borer IPM; FAO Coffee Production Guide

question: My cow's milk production dropped by half in the last week. She eats normally but her manure is watery. No vet nearby.
answer: A sudden 50 percent drop in milk with normal appetite but watery manure suggests several possibilities — none of which can be diagnosed remotely. DO NOT self-medicate. What to do: (1) Take the cow's temperature — a reading above 39.5 C suggests infection. (2) Check the udder quarters for heat, swelling, or abnormal milk — mastitis is the most common cause of milk drop. (3) Check for ticks behind ears, under tail, and between legs — ECF kills within days if untreated. (4) Call a veterinary officer — many counties have community animal health workers (CAHWs) who can visit. (5) Provide clean water, good quality hay, and mineral lick. Separate this cow from others. Save a fresh manure sample for the vet.
source: KALRO Dairy Health Guide; Kenya Veterinary Board Advisory; ILRI Animal Health Protocol

question: Maembe yangu yana madoa meusi kwenye matunda na majani. Matunda yanadondoka kabla hayajaiva.
answer: Madoa meusi kwenye matunda na majani ya maembe na kudondoka kabla ya kuiva ni dalili za ugonjwa wa anthracnose — ugonjwa wa kawaida wa maembe hasa wakati wa mvua. Haya ya kufanya: (1) KATA matawi yote yaliyoathirika na uyachome. (2) Kagua miti na UVUNE matunda yote yenye madoa na uyachome. (3) Dumisha usafi chini ya miti — kusanya na kuchoma majani na matunda yaliyooza. (4) Kwa msimu ujao, anza kunyunyizia dawa ya ukungu kabla ya kutoa maua. (5) Hakikisha miti ina nafasi ya kutosha na matawi yamepunguzwa kwa ajili ya hewa. Aina sugu ni Tommy Atkins, Keitt, na Kent.
source: KALRO Mango Production Guide; AVRDC Mango Anthracnose Management

question: Nakatong'a karanga to ayude tiyop kata gi lowo e iye. Karanga moko duto e puodho otamo nyago. Ang'o manyalo konya?
answer: Tiyop kata lowo e i karanga kod okang' mar nyago nyiso ni nitie tuo mar aflatoxin kata tuo mar lowo. Tim magi: (1) Gol karanga duto e puodho — kik icham kendo kik ius kata gima chalre kama. Aflatoxin inyalo kelo tuo mar liver ma rach. (2) Kuom seche mabiro: los sulu mag pi e puodho, keyo karanga ka gisechiek, riambo karanga e chieng' maber nyaka chop ng'ich, kan karanga e kar ma otwo. (3) Rhizobium kata Trichoderma inyalo konyo geng'o tuo mar lowo. Penj ofisa mar kilimo.
source: IITA Groundnut Aflatoxin Management; KALRO Legume Production Guide; FAO Mycotoxin Advisory

question: Nepier mara osechako kethore e lowo ka pok aywayogi. Moko osebedo gi thuolo matindo to oselokore ma rachar.
answer: Nepier ma kethore e lowo ka pok oywayi nyiso ni nitie tuo kata chandruok mar lowo. Tim magi: (1) Ne ane ka nitie tuo mar sweet potato weevil (Cylas spp.) — ma en ondiegi ma lando tuo ma golo rangi ma rachar kod thuolo e nepier. (2) Ywayo nepier mosekethore duto kendo wang'gi. (3) Kuom pitho manyien, pidh kodhi maonge tuo moa kuom ofisa mar kilimo kata KALRO. (4) Los ng'weng'o malo (ridges) mondo kik we ng'ong'o chakre e lowo ma chung' pi. (5) Gol nepier duto kinyoro ka gisechiek — kik iwe e lowo ng'iyo.
source: KALRO Sweet Potato Pest Guide; CIP Weevil Management; FAO Root Crop Advisory

question: My bananas are ripening unevenly and some have black streaks inside the fruit. The leaves are also yellowing from the edges. I grow East African Highland type.
answer: Uneven ripening, black streaks inside fruit, and leaf yellowing on East African Highland bananas are classic symptoms of banana bacterial wilt (BBW). IMMEDIATE actions: (1) Cut down and BURY the entire affected mat at least 1 meter deep — do not leave debris above ground. (2) Disinfect all tools with household bleach (jik) or flame between each plant. (3) REMOVE the male bud from healthy plants using a forked stick — never a knife. (4) Do NOT move planting material from this field. (5) Report to your district agricultural officer — Uganda has a national BBW control program. They can provide clean planting material of tolerant varieties like M9 and M19.
source: NARO Banana Bacterial Wilt Management; IITA BBW Protocol; Uganda MAAIF Extension Guide

question: Emwanyi yange ebala obulungi naye empeke zivaamu amazzi era zitera okukala. Nkozesa kasooli?
answer: Empeke ezivaamu amazzi n'okukala mu mwanyi kiyinza okuba ekiva ku ntobazi (coffee berry disease) oba coffee leaf rust. Bino by'okola: (1) TONDA empeke zonna ezigudde ne zikaze — zibike mu ttaka oba ozookye. (2) SALIRA amatabi agakalire n'ago agalina obulwadde. (3) Emwanyi gy'olina tegyetaaga kasooli — kasooli ng'obungi asobola okwonoona omutindo. (4) Kola ku kifo ky'omwanyi okubeera ekyonjo. (5) Genda eri ofiisa wa by'obulimi ow'essaza lyo — banaasobola okukulaga eddagala erisaanira. (6) Ennimiro y'emwanyi erina okubeera n'ekisiikirize ekiri wakati wa 40-50%.
source: NARO Coffee Production Guide; UCDA Extension; CABI Coffee Disease Management

question: My cassava roots are small and the leaves are curling upwards with yellow patches. I have been using stems from my own field for years.
answer: Small roots with curled leaves showing yellow patches are strong symptoms of cassava mosaic disease (CMD). Using your own stems for years has likely accumulated the virus. What to do: (1) UPROOT and burn ALL affected plants. (2) Do NOT use any stems from this field for planting. (3) Obtain CLEAN certified planting material from NARO/NACRRI or your district agricultural office — varieties like NASE 14, NASE 19, and NAROCASS 1 are resistant. (4) Rotate the field to legumes for at least one season. (5) Plant at the beginning of rains to give plants a strong start before whitefly populations build up.
source: NARO/NACRRI Cassava Program; IITA CMD Management; Uganda MAAIF Cassava Strategy

question: My cocoa pods have black patches that spread quickly during rains. Some pods turn completely black and hard. I am in Ashanti region.
answer: Black patches on cocoa pods that spread quickly in rain and turn pods black and hard is black pod disease (Phytophthora spp.). What to do: (1) REMOVE all infected pods immediately — pile them away from the farm. (2) Harvest ripe pods promptly. (3) Thin the canopy to allow more light and air circulation. (4) Remove chupons and maintain good drainage. (5) Contact your district COCOBOD extension officer — Ghana's CODAPEC program provides free fungicide spraying during the rainy season. (6) Do NOT self-mix or apply chemicals without COCOBOD guidance.
source: CRIG Black Pod Management; COCOBOD CODAPEC Program; ICCO Sustainable Cocoa Guide

question: Me yam no mu atutu na baabi a mekora no no, ebinom reye kola fitaa na won ho ada aporow. Mfaso ben na ewo so?
answer: Yam a ne mu atutu na ebinom ho aporow na aye fitaa wo baabi a wokora no ye nsonsono a efi fungal rot anaase storage nematodes. Nea ese se woye: (1) YI yam a woasee no nyinaa firi baabi a wokora no ho ntem ara. (2) HWE yam no yiye na woanye ho ade kese wo otwa bere mu. (3) ANSA worekora yam no, ma enkyene (cure) wo baabi a ewiem ye hyew na mframa nso wo ho — nna 3-5. (4) Kora yam no wo mmea a mframa fa mu yie na enye nuru. (5) Afe a ereba no, pe nhini a eda mu wo asaase mu no. (6) Ko COCOBOD ana ofisa kuaye ho.
source: CRI Yam Storage Guide; CSIR-Ghana Food Research; IITA Yam Post-Harvest Advisory

question: Ibishyimbo byanjye bifite ibibara by'umuhondo ku mababi kandi ntibikura neza. Nabibyaye nyuma y'ibirayi. Ni iki nakoze nabi?
answer: Ibibara by'umuhondo ku mababi y'ibishyimbo bikurikira guhinga ibirayi bishobora guterwa no kubura intungamubiri (azote) cyangwa indwara z'umutaka. Iby'ukora: (1) Fata urugero rw'ubutaka ujye kwa agronome. (2) Teganya guhinga ibishyimbo wongeyeho ifumbire ya DAP cyangwa NPK 17-17-17. (3) Reba niba hari udukoko twangiza imizi. (4) Gerageza kongera ifumbire ya foliar feed igizwe na azote (nka urea 1% mu mazi) — ariko banza ubaza agronome. (5) Mu gihe kizaza, jya uhinduranya ibihingwa — ntukore ibirayi n'ibishyimbo bikurikirana.
source: RAB Bean Production Guide; CIAT Rwanda Integrated Soil Fertility; FAO Crop Rotation Advisory

question: Ibigori byanjye birimo utubuye twinshi tw'umuhondo kandi ibyatsi bimaze kumera hose. Nta mafaranga mfite yo kugura imiti. Wakora iki?
answer: Utubuye tw'umuhondo nyuma yo kubyara ibigori ni ikimenyetso cya Striga (Striga hermonthica). Iki nicyo cy'ukora nta mafaranga menshi: (1) KURA Striga yose ukimara kuyibona, mbere yuko itanga imbuto. Buri giti kimwe gishobora gutanga imbuto zigera ku 50,000. (2) UKORE ibi: washe ibigori bikivangwa n'imbuto za Striga mu mazi arimo ifumbire — DAP ikingana n'ikiganza kimwe muri buri litre 10 z'amazi. (3) Tegera ibishyimbo cyangwa ubunyobwa hagati y'imirongo y'ibigori. (4) Mu gihe kizaza, jya uhinduranya ibihingwa buri mwaka. (5) Gerageza gushakisha imbuto z'ibigori zihanganira Striga — egera agronome wa RAB.
source: RAB Striga Management Program; CIMMYT Striga Control; FAO Push-Pull Technology Guide

question: Ibishyimbo byanjye biribwa n'udukoko duto dutukura tw'ijosi. Hari umuti nta kiguzi?
answer: Udusimba tw'ijosi dutukura ni aphids. Hano ni uko wabirwanya nta mafaranga: (1) Tegura amazi y'isabune y'inkari (5g ya sabuni ya materasi mu litre 1 y'amazi) hanyuma uyicishe kuri ibyo bimera. (2) Shaka ibishyimbo bitandukanye — nk'ibishyimbo by'umweru n'ibijima — byoroshya imirire y'ubutaka. (3) Ntuterane cyane — haga umwanya hagati y'ibishyimbo. (4) Koresha ibishara (mulch) nk'ibyatsi byumye kugira ngo ubutaka butinyishe amazi. (5) Niba ibishyimbo byaranduye cyane, urabe ukura kandi ukayitwika kure y'umurima.
source: RAB Bean Production Guide; CIAT Bean Pest Management

question: Ibishyimbo byanjye byera ibara ry'umuhondo kandi ntibikura neza. Byabaye iki?
answer: Ibara ry'umuhondo ku bishyimbo bishobora guterwa n'ibintu byinshi: (1) Kubura azote (nitrogen) — ibishyimbo bikora azote ubwabyo, ariko niba ubutaka bufite aside nyinshi (pH iri hasi), ntibishobora gukora neza. (2) Indwara ya virus (Bean Common Mosaic Virus) — iyi virus iterwa n'aphids. (3) Kubura amazi — ibishyimbo bikenera amazi mu gihe cyo gukura. Ingamba: (1) Ohereza ubutaka mu kigo cy'ubuhinzi (RAB) kugira ngo bapime pH. (2) Niba aside nyinshi, shyiramo ifumbire y'inka cyangwa lime. (3) Hitamo imbuto zihanganira indwara — zigwa mu biro by'ubuhinzi. (4) Jya uhinduranya ibihingwa — ntukore ibishyimbo ku murima umwe buri mwaka.
source: RAB Soil Fertility Guide; CIAT Bean Disease Management

question: Ibigori byanjye ntibikura neza n'ibibara byabyo ni ibishya, ndetse n'ibiti byabyo biroroshye. Mbona imizi yabyo ari mito. Ngize iki?
answer: Ibi byose ni ibimenyetso byo kubura fosifori (phosphorus) mu butaka. Iki ni ikibazo kenshi mu Rwanda aho ubutaka buffite aside nyinshi. (1) Ohereza ubutaka bwawe mu ishami rya RAB riri hafi yawe kugira ngo bapime. (2) Shyiramo ifumbire ikize kuri fosifori (DAP) ubwo uhinga, ikiganza kimwe ku giti cy'ibigori. (3) Koresha ifumbire y'inka cyangwa ifumbire y'ibimera (compost) — byongera ubuzima bw'ubutaka. (4) Hitamo imbuto z'ibigori zikura vuba — zikenera fosifori nke. (5) Mu gihe kizaza, kora imirongo izenguruka imisozi (contour ridging) kugira ngo ubutaka butazanywa n'amazi.
source: RAB Maize Nutrition Guide; CIMMYT Soil Fertility

question: Ibigori byanjye birimo utuntu twinshi tw'umukara ku mpusu. Ibi bintu ni ibiki?
answer: Uwo ni ugukanya k'ibigori (maize smut — Ustilago maydis). Ni indwara y'ibigori ikunze kugaragara mu Rwanda igihe cy'ubushyuhe bukabije. (1) Kura utwo tuntu mbere y'uko tumeneka — bitabarika utwo tuntu dusohora imyanda y'indwara mu butaka. (2) Twika utwo tuntu kure y'umurima — ntukabishyire mu kirundo cy'ifumbire. (3) Hinduranya ibihingwa — ntuhinge ibigori aho wabikoze umwaka ushize. (4) Hitamo imbuto zihanganira indwara nka 'PAN 691' cyangwa 'SC 403'. (5) Ntukoreshe ifumbire ya azote nyinshi — iyo ikabije ituma indwara ikura cyane.
source: RAB Maize Disease Guide; CIMMYT Smut Management

question: Ikawa yanjye ifite amabara y'umuhondo ku mababi kandi amababi arahinduka. Mbona utuntu tw'umweru munsi y'amababi. Ni iki gitari?
answer: Ibi ni ibimenyetso by'udukoko twa 'berry borer' (Hypothenemus hampei) n'utuntu tw'umweru ni indwara ya 'white stem borer'. (1) Kura amababi yose yanduye hanyuma uyature kure y'umurima.
